about: Menus served to the app at GET /v1/content/menus: named sets of 3-7 recipes with a short intro. 'kind' is weekly, occasion or mood. 'recipes' lists recipe ids from the app's library (ios/RefrigeratorRecipes/Resources/SampleRecipes.json) or the recipe packs (recipe-packs.json); a recipe in neither goes in full, with its own id, under the menu's 'recipeDetails'. Optional: 'slot' (dinner by default, or lunch) is the meal the app plans; 'Add all to plan' spreads the recipes tagged for that meal over the week and puts sides and desserts with the first, while an occasion is planned as one meal on a day the user picks; 'mood' is a mood tag id; 'window' {from, to} shows the menu on Tonight while in season, as yearly dates (MM-DD, may wrap the new year), or 'windows', a list of full dates (YYYY-MM-DD) per year for holidays that move; a recipe included by one menu may be listed by another; 'reviewNotes' records the cultural review and is never sent to the app; 'draft': true keeps a menu out of the app until someone who cooks that food has reviewed it. 'rotation' is the weekly order of 'This week's menu'. Copy describes dishes many families make, never 'the' menu for a tradition. See server/README.md.

menus.title: Taco Tuesday
menus.intro: Five ways to fill a tortilla, from 25-minute beef tacos to set-and-forget salsa verde chicken, with street-corn salad on the side.

menus.title: Meatless Monday
menus.intro: Vegetarian dinners hearty enough that nobody asks where the meat went: chickpeas, tofu, beans and a bright pesto pasta.

menus.title: Lunchbox week
menus.intro: Five packable lunches kids actually eat, most made in 15 minutes or less the night before.

menus.title: Sheet-pan week
menus.intro: One pan, a hot oven and very little washing up, five nights running.

menus.title: Budget week
menus.intro: Five filling dinners built on lentils, beans, eggs and rice, some of the cheapest protein in the store.

menus.title: Sick-day soups
menus.intro: Brothy, simple bowls that are easy to make when someone at home is feeling rough. Comforting ideas, not medical advice.

menus.title: Cozy Sunday
menus.intro: Slow braises that fill the house with good smells, and a warm cobbler to finish.

menus.title: Feeling spicy
menus.intro: Real heat from five kitchens. If you're not sure how hot you like it, add the chilies a little at a time and taste as you go.

menus.title: Ring In the New Year
menus.intro: Party bites for New Year's Eve, then the good-luck plate many Southern families eat on New Year's Day: black-eyed peas for coins, greens for dollars and cornbread for gold. Plus a few customs other families bring to the table, from late-night soba to a Greek coin cake (and twelve grapes at midnight, if that's your house).

recipeDetails.title: Toshikoshi Soba (New Year's Eve Buckwheat Noodles)
recipeDetails.summary: Soba in a hot soy-dashi broth with green onions and fish cake, the bowl many Japanese and Japanese American families eat late on New Year's Eve to see the old year out.

ingredients.name: Dried soba noodles
ingredients.note: in the Asian aisle; or frozen udon

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.note: for the broth, plus a big pot for the noodles

ingredients.name: Dashi granules
ingredients.note: such as Hon-dashi, in the Asian aisle; or 6 cups store-bought dashi in place of the water and granules

ingredients.name: Mirin
ingredients.note: sweet rice wine for cooking; or 2 tbsp sugar

ingredients.name: Kamaboko fish cake
ingredients.note: sliced; at Japanese or Asian markets, or use cooked shrimp

instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil for the noodles. In a medium pot, bring the 6 cups of water to a simmer and whisk in the dashi granules, soy sauce, mirin and sugar. Taste: it should be savory and a little sweet. Keep it hot over low heat.

Cook the soba according to the package, usually 4 to 5 minutes, stirring so the noodles don't stick. Drain and rinse under cold water, rubbing gently to wash off the starch, so the noodles stay springy.
If using spinach, drop it into the hot broth for 30 seconds to wilt. Warm the fish cake slices in the broth for a minute.
Dip the noodles into the broth or a pot of hot water to rewarm, then divide among four deep bowls.
Ladle the hot broth over, lay the fish cake and spinach on top, and scatter with green onions. Pass shichimi at the table. Many families add a piece of store-bought shrimp tempura.

recipeDetails.title: Shrimp Cocktail with Horseradish Cocktail Sauce
recipeDetails.summary: Poached, chilled jumbo shrimp on ice with a sharp homemade cocktail sauce. Make it in the afternoon and it's ready when the guests come.

ingredients.name: Jumbo shrimp
ingredients.note: 16 to 20 per pound, shell-on, deveined; thawed if frozen

ingredients.name: Lemons
ingredients.note: 1 halved for the pot, 1 cut into wedges

ingredients.name: Prepared horseradish
ingredients.note: in the refrigerated case; more if you like it hot

instructions: Fill a large pot with 3 quarts of water, squeeze in the halved lemon and drop in the halves, then add the bay leaves and salt. Bring to a boil. Set a big bowl of ice water next to the stove.
Add the shrimp, turn off the heat and let them sit 3 to 4 minutes, stirring once, until pink and just opaque in the center.
Lift them straight into the ice water for 5 minutes to stop the cooking. Drain, peel, leaving the tails on, and pat dry. Cover and chill at least 1 hour or up to 1 day.
Stir the ketchup, horseradish, lemon juice and hot sauce together. Taste and add more horseradish for a bigger kick. Chill until serving.
Pile the shrimp over a bowl of ice with the sauce in the middle and the lemon wedges around it.

recipeDetails.title: Hot Spinach Artichoke Dip
recipeDetails.summary: Bubbling, cheesy spinach and artichoke dip baked in one dish. Assemble it in the morning and bake it when the party starts.

ingredients.name: Artichoke hearts
ingredients.note: 1 can or jar in water, drained and chopped

ingredients.name: Corn tortilla chips
ingredients.note: for dipping; or celery sticks, or crackers and baguette slices if gluten is no concern

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F. Wrap the thawed spinach in a clean kitchen towel and twist hard over the sink until no more water comes out; this keeps the dip from going watery.
Beat the cream cheese, sour cream and mayonnaise in a bowl until smooth. Stir in the spinach, artichokes, garlic, Parmesan, half the mozzarella and the pepper.
Spread it in a 1-quart baking dish or 9-inch pie plate and top with the rest of the mozzarella. You can cover and refrigerate it now for up to a day; add 5 to 10 minutes to the baking.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes until bubbling at the edges and golden on top.
Let it stand 5 minutes, then serve hot with chips, crackers or vegetables.

recipeDetails.title: Vasilopita (Greek New Year's Orange Cake)
recipeDetails.summary: A tender orange-scented cake with a foil-wrapped coin hidden inside. Greek families cut it on New Year's Day, and whoever finds the coin has luck for the year.

ingredients.name: Oranges
ingredients.note: zest of both, and 2/3 cup of their juice

ingredients.name: Ground mahlab
ingredients.note: at Greek or Middle Eastern markets; or 1/4 tsp almond extract

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F. Butter a 10-inch round cake pan or springform and line the bottom with parchment. Wash a coin and wrap it tightly in a small square of foil.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt and mahlab in a bowl.
Beat the butter and sugar with a mixer for 4 to 5 minutes until pale and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the orange zest and vanilla.
Stir the orange juice and milk together. On low speed, add the flour mixture in three parts, alternating with the juice mixture, mixing just until smooth.
Spread the batter in the pan, push the wrapped coin in near the edge so it's hidden, and smooth the top.
Bake 45 to 55 minutes, until golden and a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Cool 15 minutes in the pan, then turn out and cool completely.
Dust with powdered sugar. Many families stencil the year on top with a paper cutout before dusting.
Cut it at the table so everyone gets a slice, and tell guests about the coin before they bite, especially little ones.

menus.reviewNotes: Built around the Southern New Year's Day plate, reusing the pack's Hoppin' John (bacon; many cooks use a ham hock or hog jowl instead, and Lowcountry families may serve the peas and rice separately or skip pork), collards with smoked turkey (others use cabbage for 'money', or turnip or mustard greens) and skillet cornbread. Families vary on whether peas go in the rice, leaving 3 peas or a coin under the plate, and eating the leftovers as 'Skippin' Jenny' on Jan 2. Eve bites are two very common American party staples (shrimp cocktail, hot spinach-artichoke dip). Nods: toshikoshi soba is eaten on Dec 31 by Japanese families for crossing into the new year; vasilopita is cut on Jan 1 by Greek families (St. Basil's Day; I kept religious detail out of the copy). Twelve grapes (Spanish and Latin American) get a line in the intro rather than a 'recipe'. Left out: pork and sauerkraut (Pennsylvania Dutch/German), tamales, oliebollen, tteokguk and Cuban roast pork, to stay within 7 recipes; any could be a future swap. No sweet is fixed by the Southern tradition, so the vasilopita is the dessert. Fixed-date holiday: yearly window 12-27 to 01-02 wrapping the new year, no web check needed. Hoppin' John is tagged quick/weeknight in the pack; that's fine but its title reads 'Weeknight', which may look odd on a holiday menu.

menus.title: Lunar New Year Reunion Dinner
menus.intro: Dishes many Chinese and Taiwanese families make for the New Year's Eve reunion dinner: a whole fish, dumplings, uncut long noodles and sticky nian gao, done a little differently in every region and kitchen. Vietnamese families celebrating Tết and Korean families celebrating Seollal set their own tables, with dishes like bánh chưng and tteokguk.

recipeDetails.title: Qing Zheng Yu (Steamed Whole Fish with Ginger and Scallions)
recipeDetails.summary: A whole fish steamed just until it flakes, then topped with fresh ginger, scallions, soy sauce and sizzling hot oil. Served whole, for a year with more than enough.

ingredients.name: Whole fish
ingredients.note: branzino, black sea bass or red snapper, scaled and gutted, head and tail on; or two 8 oz white fish fillets (steam 7 to 8 min)

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger
ingredients.note: peeled; half sliced into coins, half cut into fine matchsticks

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.note: 2 cut into long pieces, 4 cut into thin 3-inch shreds

ingredients.name: Shaoxing wine
ingredients.note: or dry sherry; leave out if you prefer

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.note: light or regular; a seasoned soy sauce for seafood is also common

instructions: Rinse the fish and pat it dry inside and out. Cut 2 or 3 shallow slashes down to the bone on each side so it cooks evenly. Rub with the Shaoxing wine, if using.

Set up a steamer: a wok or wide pot with a rack and a lid, with about 1 inch of water below the rack. Lay the scallion pieces and ginger coins on a heatproof plate that fits inside and set the fish on top.

Bring the water to a full boil, put the plate on the rack, cover and steam over high heat 10 to 12 minutes for a 1¾ lb fish (about 8 minutes per inch at the thickest part). It is done when the flesh at the thickest slash is opaque and lifts off the bone.
While it steams, warm the soy sauce, sugar and water in a small pan until the sugar dissolves.
Lift the plate out carefully. Pour off the steaming liquid and throw away the cooked scallion and ginger; they have done their job. Scatter the ginger matchsticks and scallion shreds over the fish.

Heat the oil in a small pan until it just starts to smoke, then pour it over the ginger and scallions so they sizzle. Spoon the warm soy sauce around (not over) the fish, add white pepper and cilantro, and serve right away.
At the table, many families eat the top side, then lift the bone away rather than flipping the fish, and leave a little over for the year ahead.

recipeDetails.title: Bai Qie Ji (White-Cut Chicken with Ginger-Scallion Sauce)
recipeDetails.summary: A whole chicken gently poached until silky, chilled in ice water for tight skin, then chopped and served with a bright ginger-scallion oil. Cantonese families often serve it at the New Year table.

ingredients.name: Whole chicken
ingredients.note: about 3½ to 4 lb; an Asian-market chicken with head and feet is traditional, a supermarket bird works fine

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger
ingredients.note: 2 inches sliced for the pot, 2 inches very finely minced for the sauce

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.note: 3 whole for the pot, 5 very finely chopped for the sauce

ingredients.name: Shaoxing wine
ingredients.note: or dry sherry; leave out if you prefer

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.note: 1 tsp for the pot, 1 tsp for the sauce, ½ tsp for the skin

instructions: Take the chicken out of the fridge 30 minutes ahead. Pull out any loose fat from the cavity and rub the skin with ½ tsp salt.
Choose a pot that holds the chicken snugly and fill it with enough water to cover the bird. Add the sliced ginger, whole scallions, 1 tsp salt and the Shaoxing wine, if using, and bring to a boil.

Holding the chicken by the wings or with a big spoon in the cavity, dip it into the boiling water and lift it out three times so the cavity fills with hot water. Then lower it in breast side up and bring back to a bare simmer.

Simmer very gently 15 minutes, then cover, turn off the heat and let it sit 30 to 35 minutes. Check the thickest part of the thigh with an instant-read thermometer: it should read 165°F. If not, simmer a few minutes more and check again.

Meanwhile fill a large bowl with ice and cold water. Lift the chicken out, draining the cavity, and plunge it in the ice bath for 10 to 15 minutes. This sets the skin and keeps the meat juicy. Keep the poaching broth for soup or the greens.

For the sauce, put the minced ginger, chopped scallions and 1 tsp salt in a heatproof bowl. Heat the neutral oil until it shimmers and just starts to smoke, then pour it over; it will sizzle. Stir and let cool.

Pat the chicken dry and brush it with sesame oil. Chop through the bone into pieces with a cleaver, or carve it into legs, wings and sliced breast, and arrange it back in the shape of the bird. Serve at room temperature with the ginger-scallion sauce.

recipeDetails.title: Zhu Rou Bai Cai Jiaozi (Pork and Napa Cabbage Dumplings)
recipeDetails.summary: Juicy pork and napa cabbage dumplings, folded together the way many northern Chinese families do on New Year's Eve, boiled and dipped in black vinegar. Extras freeze well.

ingredients.name: Napa cabbage
ingredients.note: about half a medium head, very finely chopped

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.note: 1 tsp for the cabbage, ½ tsp for the filling

ingredients.name: Ground pork
ingredients.note: not extra-lean; 20 to 30 percent fat keeps it juicy

ingredients.name: Shaoxing wine
ingredients.note: or dry sherry; leave out if you prefer

ingredients.name: Round dumpling wrappers
ingredients.note: about a 1 lb package, refrigerated or thawed frozen; at Asian markets and many supermarkets near the tofu

ingredients.name: Chinese black vinegar
ingredients.note: Chinkiang vinegar; or rice vinegar with a few drops of balsamic

instructions: Toss the chopped cabbage with 1 tsp salt and let it sit 15 minutes. Squeeze it hard by handfuls (or in a clean towel) to get out as much water as you can.

In a large bowl, mix the pork with the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine (if using), ½ tsp salt and white pepper. Stir in one direction with chopsticks, adding the broth a spoonful at a time, until the meat looks sticky and has absorbed it, 2 to 3 minutes.
Fold in the squeezed cabbage, scallions, ginger and sesame oil. Fry a teaspoon of filling to taste for salt if you like.

To fold, put about 1 tablespoon of filling in the center of a wrapper. Wet half the edge with water, fold it over into a half-moon and pinch the middle shut. Pleat or press from the middle toward each end, pushing out the air. Keep finished dumplings on a floured tray, not touching, under a towel.

Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Add 12 to 15 dumplings and stir gently so they don't stick. When it returns to a boil, add 1 cup cold water. Repeat twice more; when the dumplings float and look puffy after the third boil, they're done, about 8 minutes in all.
Lift them out with a slotted spoon. Mix the black vinegar with a splash of soy sauce and the garlic and chili oil, if using, for dipping.
To freeze extras, freeze them on the tray until hard, then bag them. Boil from frozen with one extra addition of cold water.

recipeDetails.title: Chang Shou Mian (Long-Life Noodles with Shiitake and Chives)
recipeDetails.summary: Long, uncut noodles stir-fried with shiitake mushrooms and garlic chives in a savory oyster sauce glaze. The longer the noodle, the longer the life, so nobody cuts them.

ingredients.name: Yi mein noodles
ingredients.note: dried longevity noodles; or fresh lo mein egg noodles, or dried thin wheat noodles

ingredients.name: Dark soy sauce
ingredients.note: for color; or more regular soy sauce

instructions: Soak the dried shiitake in 1 cup hot water for 30 minutes, until soft. Squeeze them out over the bowl, keep ½ cup of the soaking liquid, cut off the stems and slice the caps.
Stir the oyster sauce, soy sauce, dark soy sauce (if using), sugar and ½ cup mushroom liquid together in a small bowl.

Cook the noodles in boiling water according to the package, usually 2 to 4 minutes, just until tender; don't break or cut them. Drain, rinse briefly under cold water, shake dry and toss with 1 tsp of the sesame oil.
Heat a wok or large skillet over high heat with the neutral oil. Add the garlic and mushrooms and stir-fry 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the noodles and the sauce. Toss with tongs or chopsticks, lifting the noodles high so they coat evenly, until the sauce is absorbed, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the chives and bean sprouts, if using, and toss 1 minute more until just wilted. Drizzle with the rest of the sesame oil and pile the noodles onto a platter long and whole.

recipeDetails.title: Chang Nian Cai (Taiwanese Long-Year Mustard Greens)
recipeDetails.summary: Whole mustard greens simmered in broth with garlic, leaves left long and uncut. Many Taiwanese families eat them on New Year's Eve for a long life, and their gentle bitterness balances a rich table.

ingredients.name: Chinese mustard greens
ingredients.note: gai choy, at Asian markets; or Shanghai bok choy, or curly mustard greens (more peppery)

ingredients.name: Chicken broth
ingredients.note: or the poaching broth from white-cut chicken, or vegetable broth

instructions: Separate the mustard green stalks and wash well, as grit hides at the base. Leave the leaves whole; if the stalks are very thick, split them lengthwise so they cook evenly.
Heat the oil in a wide pot or deep skillet over medium heat and cook the garlic 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the broth, salt and sugar and bring to a boil. Add the greens, thick stalks first, and press them under.
Cover and simmer 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until the stalks are tender and the greens are a deep, soft green. Taste the broth for salt.
Lay the greens on a platter as long as they are, spoon some broth over and drizzle with sesame oil if you like.

recipeDetails.title: Nian Gao (Cantonese Brown Sugar Sticky Rice Cake)
recipeDetails.summary: A chewy, glossy steamed cake of sweet rice flour and brown sugar, made ahead for the New Year because its name sounds like 'higher each year'. Eat it sliced, or pan-fry slices until crisp.

ingredients.name: Glutinous rice flour
ingredients.note: also sold as sweet rice flour (Erawan green bag or Mochiko); regular rice flour won't work

ingredients.name: Dark brown sugar
ingredients.note: packed; or about 10 oz Chinese brown slab sugar

ingredients.name: Dried red dates
ingredients.note: jujubes, pitted and halved, for the top

instructions: Stir the brown sugar into the hot water until fully dissolved, then let it cool until just warm.

Put the glutinous rice flour in a large bowl and slowly pour in the sugar water, stirring, until you have a smooth, thick batter with no lumps, like heavy pancake batter. Stir in 2 tbsp oil. Strain it through a sieve if any lumps remain.
Oil an 8-inch round cake pan or heatproof bowl and line the bottom with parchment. Pour in the batter, tap it on the counter to release bubbles and arrange the red dates on top if using.

Set up a large steamer with plenty of water (a wok or stockpot with a rack works). Cover the pan loosely with foil or lay a towel under the lid so condensation doesn't drip on the cake. Steam over medium-high heat 60 to 75 minutes, topping up with boiling water every 20 minutes, until the cake looks dark and glossy all the way through and a chopstick in the center comes out sticky but not milky.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds if using, then let it cool completely, uncovered, at least 6 hours or overnight. It sets firm as it cools.

Loosen the edge with an oiled knife and turn it out. Slice with an oiled knife and eat as is, or for the days after New Year, cut ½-inch slices, dip in beaten egg if you like, and pan-fry in a little oil 2 minutes per side until crisp outside and soft inside.
Keeps wrapped at room temperature 2 days, in the fridge about 2 weeks (it hardens; pan-frying softens it again), or frozen in slices up to 3 months.

menus.reviewNotes: Focus: a Chinese/Taiwanese reunion dinner (年夜飯), mixing northern dumplings with Cantonese steamed fish, white-cut chicken, yi mein and brown-sugar nian gao, plus Taiwanese chang nian cai; the intro says so and names Tết and Seollal as separate traditions rather than folding in token dishes. Second-cook review: fish is served whole and not flipped, steaming liquid is discarded, noodles are never cut, and the chicken is cooked to 165°F in the thigh (many Cantonese cooks stop earlier with pink bone; we chose the US-safe target). Families vary a lot: Shanghainese households make ningbo-style rice cake stir-fries and fried spring rolls, Fujianese and Taiwanese tables often have a hot pot or buddha-jumps-over-the-wall, northern families may skip fish and chicken and just make a mountain of dumplings, some hide a clean coin in one dumpling (left out as a choking risk), and nian gao comes in many forms (Shanghai sliced rice cake, Taiwanese red-bean, coconut). Left out: fried spring rolls (deep-frying for a big meal at home, and the menu already has a folded dumpling), tangyuan (more Lantern Festival/Winter Solstice), and Tết/Seollal dishes like bánh chưng, thịt kho trứng and tteokguk, which deserve their own menus. No library recipes reused: the closest (lo mein, three-cup chicken, caramel fish) are fine dishes but not what these families put on this table. Dates: computed day 1 of month 1 with the lunardate Python package (2027-02-06, 2028-01-26) and confirmed by web search (history.com/publicholidays for China, Vietnamese sources for Tết). Korean Seollal differs by a day because Korea's calendar uses UTC+9: Korean sources give 2027-02-07 (public holiday Feb 6-9) and 2028-01-27 (holiday Jan 26-28), so each window opens 13 days before the Chinese date and closes after the Korean holiday. The next one after that is 2029-02-13, outside the range.

menus.title: An Iftar to Share
menus.intro: Dishes many Muslim families set out when the fast breaks at sunset: dates and water first, then lentil soup, samosas and akara, a pot of biryani, and qatayef with tea. Every table differs by country and family, and the meat is halal throughout, so mix and match.

recipeDetails.title: Keema Samosas (Beef Sambusa)
recipeDetails.summary: Crisp triangles of spiced ground beef and peas folded in spring roll wrappers, the shortcut many Pakistani and East African home cooks swear by. Medium heat.

ingredients.name: Ground beef
ingredients.note: halal, 85% lean; or ground lamb or chicken

ingredients.name: Vegetable oil
ingredients.note: for the filling, plus more for frying

ingredients.name: Spring roll wrappers
ingredients.note: 8-inch square, thawed, from the freezer aisle at Asian grocers; or samosa pastry sheets (patti) from South Asian grocers, or egg roll wrappers

ingredients.name: All-purpose flour
ingredients.note: mixed with 2 tbsp water to seal

ingredients.name: Tamarind chutney
ingredients.note: for dipping; or green chutney or ketchup

instructions: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, ginger and serranos and cook 1 minute.
Add the beef and cook, breaking it up finely, 8 to 10 minutes until browned and any liquid has cooked off. Stir in the cumin, coriander, garam masala and salt and cook 1 minute more.
Stir in the peas, cilantro and lemon juice, taste for salt, then spread on a plate to cool completely. A dry, cool filling keeps the wrappers crisp.

Cut each wrapper in half into two long strips and keep them under a damp towel. Fold one end of a strip over to make a triangle pocket, fill with a heaping tablespoon of beef, then keep folding the triangle up the strip like a flag. Seal the last flap with flour paste.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a heavy pot to 350°F. Fry the samosas a few at a time for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until golden and blistered. Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with chutney. To bake instead, brush with oil and bake at 400°F for 18 to 20 minutes, turning once. Uncooked samosas freeze well on a tray; fry from frozen, adding a minute.

recipeDetails.title: Akara (Black-Eyed Pea Fritters)
recipeDetails.summary: Fluffy, crisp-edged fritters of whipped black-eyed peas, onion and hot pepper, loved at iftar in Nigeria and as accara in Senegal. Soak the peas overnight.

ingredients.name: Habanero pepper
ingredients.note: or Scotch bonnet; use half for milder

ingredients.name: Yellow onion
ingredients.note: finely diced, folded in at the end

instructions: Rub the soaked peas between your palms in a big bowl of water so the skins float up; skim them off and repeat until most peas are skinless. A few skins left behind are fine.
Blend the peas with the chopped onion and habanero, adding water a spoonful at a time, until you have a thick, smooth paste like stiff pancake batter.
Scrape into a bowl and beat hard with a wooden spoon or a hand mixer for 3 to 4 minutes until it lightens and looks fluffy. Stir in the salt and the diced onion if using.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a heavy pot to 350°F. Drop in heaping tablespoons of batter, a few at a time, and fry 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and puffed.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot, on their own or tucked into bread. Some families serve them with pap (ogi) or kunu.

recipeDetails.title: Stuffed Medjool Dates with Walnuts and Tahini
recipeDetails.summary: Soft Medjool dates filled with toasted walnuts, drizzled with tahini and scattered with pistachios: a little plate for breaking the fast, set out with water.

ingredients.name: Orange blossom water
ingredients.note: in the Middle Eastern aisle; skip if you can't find it

instructions: Toast the walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until fragrant, then let them cool.
Slit each date lengthwise down one side and pull out the pit, keeping the date in one piece.
Press a walnut half into each date and pinch it closed around the nut. Arrange on a plate.
Loosen the tahini with the orange blossom water and a teaspoon of warm water if it is thick, then drizzle over the dates and scatter with pistachios and a pinch of salt.
Set out before sunset with a pitcher of water, plus a bowl of plain dates for anyone who prefers them simple. They keep covered at room temperature for a day.

recipeDetails.title: Qatayef (Walnut-Stuffed Pancakes)
recipeDetails.summary: Little yeasted pancakes cooked on one side, folded around cinnamon walnuts, baked crisp and soaked in orange blossom syrup. A Ramadan sweet across the Levant and Egypt.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: divided: 1 tbsp for the batter, 2 tbsp for the filling, the rest for the syrup

ingredients.name: Warm water
ingredients.note: 1 1/4 cups for the batter, 1/2 cup for the syrup

ingredients.name: Butter
ingredients.note: melted; or ghee or vegetable oil

ingredients.name: Orange blossom water
ingredients.note: in the Middle Eastern aisle; or rose water, or 1/2 tsp vanilla

instructions: Make the syrup first so it can cool: simmer 1 cup sugar and 1/2 cup water for 8 minutes until slightly thick, stir in the lemon juice and orange blossom water, and let it cool.
Whisk the flour, semolina, 1 tbsp sugar, yeast, baking powder and salt with 1 1/4 cups warm water into a smooth batter like thin pancake batter. Cover and rest 30 minutes until bubbly.
Mix the walnuts, cinnamon and 2 tbsp sugar for the filling.

Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat; no oil. Pour 2 tbsp of batter per pancake to make 3- to 4-inch rounds. Cook on one side only, about 2 minutes, until the top is covered in holes and looks dry. Do not flip. Stack them under a towel.
Heat the oven to 400°F. Put a spoonful of filling on the bubbly side of each pancake, fold in half and pinch the edges firmly to seal. Set on a sheet pan and brush with melted butter.
Bake 15 to 18 minutes until crisp and golden, then dip each hot qatayef in the cool syrup, or spoon it over. Serve warm or at room temperature.

menus.reviewNotes: Second-cook review: the table follows how many iftars actually run: dates and water to break the fast, then soup, fried snacks, one main and a sweet, drawn from Pakistani (biryani, keema samosas), Turkish (mercimek çorbası, reused from the library), Nigerian/Senegalese (akara) and Levantine/Egyptian (stuffed dates, qatayef) home cooking. Halal: no pork, no alcohol, no wine-based condiments. I skipped the library's chicken yassa because its Dijon mustard is often made with white wine. The ground beef note says halal, and the intro says the meat is halal throughout, because the reused biryani lists plain chicken thighs. Families vary a lot. Moroccan homes would serve harira with chebakia; Gulf and Somali tables have sambusa and harees; South Asian iftars add pakoras, fruit chaat, dahi bhalla and Rooh Afza; Turkish homes have pide and güllaç. I left out harira so the menu doesn't have two soups, and left out drinks such as jallab, qamar al-din and bissap because the schema has no drink tag. Dates were checked by web search on 2026-10-02 (islamicfinder, anycalendar, truecalendar and others; the Fiqh Council of North America calendar is listed). Ramadan 1448 is expected from about Feb 8 to Mar 9, 2027, with Eid around Mar 10. Ramadan 1449 is expected from about Jan 28 to Feb 26/27, 2028, with Eid around Feb 27/28. Each window opens about 13 days before day one and closes a day or two after Eid, with ±1–2 days of slack for moon sighting. Ramadan 2026 (Feb–Mar 2026) ended before October 2026, so it has no window.

menus.title: Eid al-Fitr Feast
menus.intro: Dishes many families make for the big Eid al-Fitr meal: a slow-cooked korma, seekh kebabs, cool dahi baray, sheer khurma for Eid morning and date-filled maamoul for guests. Every family's table is different, from Lahore to Beirut to Jakarta, so mix in your own favorites.

recipeDetails.title: Shahi Lamb Korma
recipeDetails.summary: A rich, mild Pakistani-style korma: bone-in lamb slow-cooked in yogurt with browned onions, whole spices and ground almonds. Better made the day before.

ingredients.name: Bone-in lamb shoulder
ingredients.note: cut into 2-inch pieces (ask the butcher); bone-in goat from a halal butcher is traditional

ingredients.name: Yellow onions
ingredients.note: thinly sliced; or 1 1/2 cups store-bought fried onions (birista)

ingredients.name: Green cardamom pods
ingredients.note: lightly crushed; or 1/2 tsp ground cardamom

ingredients.name: Kashmiri chili powder
ingredients.note: for color, mild; or 1 tsp paprika plus a pinch of cayenne

ingredients.name: Ground almonds
ingredients.note: almond flour works; or blend 1/3 cup cashews with a little water

ingredients.name: Kewra water
ingredients.note: screwpine water from South Asian grocers; or rose water

instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Fry the onions, stirring often, 15 to 18 minutes until evenly deep golden. Lift them out onto a plate, leaving the oil behind, and let them crisp.

Add the cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaves to the hot oil and stir 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the lamb and salt and sear on medium-high, turning, about 10 minutes until the meat is browned in spots.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook 2 minutes. Crumble in two-thirds of the fried onions, then add the coriander and chili powder and stir 1 minute.

Take the pot off the heat for a minute so the yogurt won't split, then stir in the yogurt a spoonful at a time. Return to medium heat and cook, stirring, 5 minutes until the oil starts to glisten at the edges.
Add the hot water, cover and simmer on low for 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 hours, stirring every 20 minutes, until the lamb is very tender and comes away from the bone.
Stir in the ground almonds and garam masala and simmer uncovered 5 to 10 minutes until the sauce is thick and creamy, with a layer of oil on top. Taste for salt.
Sprinkle with the kewra water and drizzle with ghee if using, scatter over the rest of the fried onions, and serve with naan, sheermal or rice. It reheats beautifully the next day.

recipeDetails.title: Dahi Baray (Lentil Dumplings in Spiced Yogurt)
recipeDetails.summary: Soft urad dal dumplings soaked and nestled in sweetened yogurt with chaat masala and tamarind chutney. Soak the dal the night before; assemble ahead and serve cold.

ingredients.name: Urad dal
ingredients.note: split, skinless white lentils from South Asian grocers or Amazon; soak 6 hours or overnight; or use moong dal

ingredients.name: Chaat masala
ingredients.note: South Asian grocers or the spice aisle; or mix ground cumin, dried mango powder and black salt

ingredients.name: Tamarind chutney
ingredients.note: jarred, from South Asian grocers; or simmer tamarind paste with sugar

instructions: Drain the soaked dal and blend with the ginger and 2 to 4 tbsp water into a thick, smooth batter. Beat it with a spoon or whisk for 3 to 4 minutes until light and fluffy; a dab dropped in water should float. Stir in the cumin seeds and 1 tsp salt.

Heat the oil in a deep, heavy pot to 350°F (about 1 1/2 inches deep). With wet fingers, drop in tablespoons of batter, 6 to 8 at a time, and deep-fry 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until light golden and cooked through. Drain on paper towels.
Fill a large bowl with warm water and a pinch of salt. Drop the fried dumplings in and soak 15 to 20 minutes until soft and swollen.
Whisk the yogurt with the milk, sugar and remaining 1/2 tsp salt until smooth and pourable.
Gently squeeze each dumpling between your palms to press out the water without breaking it, and lay them in a shallow serving dish.
Pour the yogurt over to cover. Chill at least 1 hour or up to a day.
Just before serving, sprinkle with chaat masala, toasted cumin and chili powder, and drizzle with tamarind chutney and cilantro if using.

recipeDetails.title: Sheer Khurma (Vermicelli and Date Milk Pudding)
recipeDetails.summary: Toasted vermicelli simmered in cardamom milk with dates, nuts and raisins: the sweet many South Asian families serve on Eid morning and to every guest after.

ingredients.name: Fine vermicelli
ingredients.note: seviyan, broken into 2-inch pieces; from South Asian grocers, or broken angel hair pasta

ingredients.name: Medjool dates
ingredients.note: pitted and chopped; dried dates (chhuhare) soaked overnight are traditional

instructions: Melt the ghee in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Fry the almonds, pistachios and cashews 2 to 3 minutes until lightly golden, add the raisins for 30 seconds until puffed, then scoop everything out, leaving the ghee.
Add the vermicelli to the ghee and stir constantly 2 to 3 minutes until evenly golden brown. Watch it closely; it burns fast.
Pour in the milk and add the cardamom. Bring to a boil, stirring so nothing sticks, then lower the heat.
Simmer, stirring often and scraping the bottom, 25 to 30 minutes until the milk has reduced by about a quarter and turned creamy.
Stir in the sugar, chopped dates and most of the fried nuts and raisins, and simmer 5 minutes more. Add the saffron milk and rose water if using.
Serve warm or chilled, topped with the remaining nuts. It thickens as it stands; loosen with a splash of milk when reheating.

recipeDetails.title: Maamoul (Date-Filled Semolina Cookies)
recipeDetails.summary: Buttery semolina cookies scented with orange blossom and rose water, wrapped around spiced date paste and pressed into patterns. Many Arab families bake them together before Eid.

ingredients.name: Fine semolina
ingredients.note: Bob's Red Mill or Middle Eastern grocers; or farina (Cream of Wheat)

ingredients.name: Mahlab
ingredients.note: ground cherry pits, from Middle Eastern grocers; or a drop of almond extract

ingredients.name: Orange blossom water
ingredients.note: Middle Eastern grocers or the baking aisle; or 1 tsp orange zest

ingredients.name: Date paste
ingredients.note: from Middle Eastern grocers; or blitz pitted Medjool dates in a food processor

instructions: In a large bowl, mix the semolina, flour, sugar and mahlab if using. Pour in the melted ghee and rub it in with your fingertips until every grain is coated and it feels like damp sand. Cover and leave at room temperature at least 2 hours, or overnight, so the semolina softens.

Mix the orange blossom water, rose water and warm milk with the yeast if using. Sprinkle it over the semolina and knead gently just until it holds together as a soft dough; don't overwork it. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
Knead the date paste with the butter, cinnamon and cardamom until smooth, then roll into 30 small balls, about 1/2 oz each.
Heat the oven to 375°F and line two sheet pans with parchment.

Take a walnut-size piece of dough, flatten it into a cup in your palm, set a date ball inside and pinch the dough closed around it. Press into a floured maamoul mold and tap it out, or shape into a smooth dome and decorate the top with a fork or tweezers.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes until the bottoms are golden; the tops should stay pale. Cool completely on the pan, as they are fragile while warm.
Dust lightly with powdered sugar if you like. They keep 2 weeks in an airtight tin, and freeze well for a month.

menus.reviewNotes: Built around a South Asian (Pakistani/North Indian Muslim) Eid table, the one I know from my own family: korma as the centerpiece with seekh kebabs alongside, dahi baray as the cooling side, and sheer khurma, which is THE Eid sweet in many of those homes (served from the morning on). Maamoul is added as the sweet many Arab families bake before Eid, so the menu nods to that tradition without pretending to be a full Levantine spread; the intro says tables differ by region. Reused the library's Oven-Baked Seekh Kebabs. Biryani is just as common at Eid, but the library biryani is already on the ramadan-iftar menu, so I left it off to keep the two menus distinct; families can add it. Deliberately avoided iftar staples (pakoras, samosas, fruit chaat, soup, dates to break the fast) so this reads as the celebration, not a regular iftar; dahi baray do appear at iftar too, but they're a fixture on Eid tables. Everything is halal: no pork or alcohol; buy lamb/chicken from a halal butcher if that matters to the household; kewra/rose/orange blossom waters are alcohol-free. Families vary on goat vs lamb vs chicken korma, sheer khurma thickness and whether to use dried dates (chhuhare), and maamoul fillings (dates, walnuts, pistachios). Left out Indonesian/Malay (rendang, ketupat), Turkish (baklava) and West African tables for focus; they'd make good separate menus. Dates: WebSearch (awarenessdays.com, publicholidays.ae, calendardate.com) gives expected Eid al-Fitr on Tue 9 March 2027 and Sun 27 Feb 2028 (2026's fell on 20 March, before October). Windows open ~12 days before and close 2-3 days after the expected date to allow for moon sighting a day earlier or later (2028 window accounts for Feb 29).

menus.title: Holi Festival Spread
menus.intro: Dishes many families make for Holi, the spring festival of colors: a big pot of chole, dahi vada and papdi chaat to snack on between rounds of color, gujiya and Maharashtrian puran poli, and cold thandai made without bhang. Every region and household has its own favorites, so treat this as a starting point.

recipeDetails.title: Punjabi Chole for a Crowd
recipeDetails.summary: Chickpeas simmered dark and tangy in an onion-tomato masala, with a tea bag for color. Many families make a big pot for Holi to eat with puri, bhature or rice; it's even better made a day ahead.

ingredients.name: Chickpeas
ingredients.note: 15 oz each, drained and rinsed (or 1 1/2 cups dried, soaked overnight and cooked)

ingredients.name: Black tea bag
ingredients.note: any plain black tea; it only adds the deep brown color

ingredients.name: Serrano chile
ingredients.note: slit lengthwise; use 2 for more heat, or skip for kids

ingredients.name: Chana masala spice blend
ingredients.note: sold at Indian grocers and many US supermarkets (MDH or Everest); or 2 tsp garam masala plus 1 tsp extra ground coriander

ingredients.name: Kashmiri chili powder
ingredients.note: mild and bright red; or 3/4 tsp paprika plus a pinch of cayenne

ingredients.name: Amchur (dried mango powder)
ingredients.note: or the juice of 1 lemon added at the end

instructions: Simmer the chickpeas with the water and the tea bag for 10 minutes, then lift out the tea bag. Keep the chickpeas in their dark water.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and bay leaf and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add the onions with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring often, 12 to 15 minutes until deep golden brown. Don't rush this; the color of the gravy comes from here.

Stir in the ginger, garlic and chile for 1 minute, then the tomatoes, chana masala, coriander, turmeric, chili powder and salt. Cook 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until the paste thickens and the oil shines at the edges.
Pour in the chickpeas with their water. Simmer uncovered 15 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas against the side of the pot to thicken the gravy. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Stir in the amchur, taste for salt, and scatter with cilantro. Serve hot with puri, bhature or rice, and lemon wedges. It keeps 3 days in the fridge and reheats well.

recipeDetails.title: Dahi Vada (Lentil Dumplings in Yogurt)
recipeDetails.summary: Soft fried urad dal dumplings under cool sweetened yogurt, tamarind chutney and roasted cumin. A Holi favorite in many North Indian homes (dahi bhalle in Punjab). Soak the dal 4 hours or overnight first.

ingredients.name: Urad dal (split, hulled black gram)
ingredients.note: from Indian grocers; soaked 4 hours or overnight. No real substitute; moong dal makes a lighter vada

ingredients.name: Green chile
ingredients.note: serrano or Thai, minced; optional for kids

ingredients.name: Plain whole-milk yogurt
ingredients.note: not Greek; or thin Greek yogurt with milk

ingredients.name: Ground cumin
ingredients.note: toasted in a dry pan until fragrant

ingredients.name: Chaat masala
ingredients.note: tangy spice blend from Indian grocers; or a pinch of black salt and amchur

ingredients.name: Tamarind chutney
ingredients.note: store-bought (imli or saunth chutney) or homemade

instructions: Drain the soaked dal and grind it in a blender with as little water as you can (2 to 4 tbsp) into a thick, fluffy paste. Beat it by hand for 3 to 4 minutes to trap air; a dab dropped in water should float.
Stir in the ginger, chile and 1 tsp salt.

Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F. With wet fingers, drop in walnut-sized spoonfuls of batter, 6 or 7 at a time, and deep-fry 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through. Drain on paper towels.

Drop the hot vadas into a large bowl of warm water with a pinch of salt and soak 15 to 20 minutes until soft and swollen. Squeeze each one gently between your palms to press out the water without breaking it.
Whisk the yogurt with the sugar and remaining 1/2 tsp salt until smooth and pourable. Lay the vadas in a shallow dish and pour the yogurt over to cover.
Chill at least 1 hour or overnight. To serve, drizzle with tamarind and green chutney and sprinkle with roasted cumin, chili powder, chaat masala and cilantro.

recipeDetails.title: Papdi Chaat with Tamarind and Mint Chutneys
recipeDetails.summary: Crisp papdi crackers piled with potato and chickpeas, cool yogurt, sweet tamarind and green chutneys, sev and pomegranate. A street-food snack many families set out at Holi gatherings, assembled just before eating.

ingredients.name: Papdi
ingredients.note: flat fried flour crackers from Indian grocers; or sturdy pita chips

ingredients.name: Chaat masala
ingredients.note: or a mix of ground cumin, amchur and a pinch of black salt

ingredients.name: Sev
ingredients.note: thin chickpea-flour noodles from Indian grocers; or crushed plain potato chips

instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water 18 to 20 minutes until tender. Cool, peel and cut into small cubes. Toss with the chickpeas, half the chaat masala and the salt.
Whisk the yogurt with the sugar until smooth and pourable.
Just before serving, lay the papdi on a platter or individual plates, 6 or 7 per person, overlapping a little.
Spoon the potato and chickpeas over them, then the yogurt. Drizzle generously with tamarind chutney and a little green chutney.
Scatter with onion, roasted cumin, chili powder, the rest of the chaat masala, sev, pomegranate and cilantro. Serve right away, before the papdi softens.

recipeDetails.title: Puran Poli (Sweet Lentil Flatbread)
recipeDetails.summary: Soft wheat flatbreads stuffed with chana dal cooked down with jaggery and cardamom, served with plenty of ghee. Maharashtrian families especially make it for Holi; many make the filling the day before.

ingredients.name: Chana dal (split Bengal gram)
ingredients.note: rinsed and soaked 1 to 2 hours; from Indian grocers, or yellow split peas

ingredients.name: Jaggery
ingredients.note: grated or chopped, from Indian grocers; or packed dark brown sugar

ingredients.name: Whole wheat flour (atta)
ingredients.note: Indian chapati flour; or regular whole wheat flour

ingredients.name: Ghee
ingredients.note: for cooking and serving; or melted butter

instructions: Make the dough: mix the atta, all-purpose flour, turmeric and salt. Add water a little at a time and knead to a very soft, sticky dough, softer than for roti. Knead in 2 tbsp oil, cover with the rest of the oil and rest at least 1 hour.
Cook the soaked dal in 3 cups water about 30 minutes until soft enough to crush between your fingers but not mushy. Drain well (save the liquid for dal or soup).

Return the dal to the pot with the jaggery over medium-low heat. Stir constantly 15 to 20 minutes as the jaggery melts and the mixture thickens; it's ready when a spoon stands up in it. Stir in cardamom and nutmeg.
While warm, mash the filling smooth with a potato masher or pulse it in a food processor. Cool completely; it firms up as it cools. Divide into 10 balls.

Divide the dough into 10 balls. Flatten one into a 4-inch disc, set a filling ball in the middle, and pull the edges up to seal it. Flatten, dust well with flour, and roll gently to a 7-inch circle. If filling peeks out, patch it with flour.

Cook on a hot dry skillet or tava over medium heat about 1 1/2 minutes per side, until golden spots appear. Brush both sides with ghee as it finishes. Stack in a towel-lined dish and serve warm with more ghee on top, or with warm milk.

recipeDetails.title: Gujiya (Sweet Khoya-Filled Pastries)
recipeDetails.summary: Crisp crescent pastries filled with khoya, coconut, nuts and cardamom. They are the Holi sweet in many North Indian homes, often made together by the whole family. Fried as is traditional, or baked for an easier batch.

ingredients.name: Ghee
ingredients.note: melted, for the dough; or melted butter

ingredients.name: Khoya (mawa)
ingredients.note: milk solids, fresh or frozen from Indian grocers; or 1 cup whole-milk ricotta cooked down in a dry pan until crumbly

ingredients.name: Vegetable oil
ingredients.note: for deep frying; or skip and bake

instructions: Rub the ghee into the flour with your fingertips until it holds together when squeezed. Add cold water a little at a time and knead to a firm, smooth dough. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
Crumble the khoya into a dry skillet over low heat and stir 5 to 7 minutes until lightly golden and fragrant. Cool until just warm, then mix in the sugar, coconut, nuts, raisins and cardamom.

Divide the dough into 20 balls and roll each into a 4-inch circle. Put a heaped tablespoon of filling on one half, wet the edge with water, fold over and press firmly to seal. Pinch and pleat the edge, or trim it with a gujiya mold or fork. Keep the rest covered as you work.
To fry: heat the oil to 300°F, lower than usual, and fry 4 or 5 at a time for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until evenly golden and crisp. Too hot and they blister. Drain on paper towels.
To bake instead: brush with melted ghee and bake on a lined sheet at 375°F for 20 to 25 minutes until golden.
Cool completely before storing. They keep 1 week in an airtight tin.

recipeDetails.title: Thandai (Spiced Almond Milk, No Bhang)
recipeDetails.summary: Cold milk blended with almonds, fennel, pepper, cardamom, rose and saffron, the cooling drink of Holi. Some adults add bhang (a cannabis preparation); this recipe has none and is for the whole family.

ingredients.name: Melon seeds (magaz)
ingredients.note: from Indian grocers; or shelled pumpkin seeds or cashews

ingredients.name: White poppy seeds
ingredients.note: khus khus; or more melon seeds

ingredients.name: Dried rose petals
ingredients.note: edible, from Indian or Middle Eastern grocers; or 1/2 tsp rose water

ingredients.name: Whole milk
ingredients.note: cold; or unsweetened almond milk for dairy-free

instructions: Soak the almonds, melon seeds, fennel, poppy seeds, peppercorns, cardamom seeds and rose petals in 1/2 cup hot water for at least 2 hours, or overnight in the fridge.
Warm 1/2 cup of the milk and steep the saffron in it.
Blend the soaked mix with its water into a very smooth paste, adding a splash of milk as needed.
Stir the paste into the remaining milk with the sugar and saffron milk. Strain through a fine sieve or cheesecloth, pressing hard on the solids.
Chill at least 1 hour. Stir and serve cold, over ice if you like. This recipe contains no bhang. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

menus.reviewNotes: Gujiya, dahi vada/dahi bhalle and thandai are the Holi foods most North Indian (UP, Bihar, Punjab, Delhi) families would name; puran poli is the Maharashtrian Holi sweet, and chole with puri or bhature is a common crowd main, so I added it so 'Add all to plan' has a dinner. Papdi chaat stands in for the many chaats (aloo tikki, bhalla papdi) families set out. Thandai is explicitly bhang-free in the title, summary and steps. Everything is vegetarian, and only the chole uses onion and garlic. Families vary a lot: some make malpua, kanji vada, namak pare/mathri, kachori, or Bengali Dol Jatra sweets; I left those out to keep it to 6 recipes. I used store-bought tamarind and green chutneys to keep the chaat realistic for a home cook, left asafoetida out of the dahi vada so it stays gluten-free, and did not tag the chole gluten-free because store-bought chana masala blends often contain hing cut with wheat flour, and gave a ricotta substitute for khoya and baked option for gujiya. Dates: Rangwali Holi/Dhulandi is Mon 22 Mar 2027 (Holika Dahan 21 Mar) and Sat 11 Mar 2028 (Holika Dahan 10 Mar), confirmed by web search (drikpanchang.com and other panchang sites; matches my own expectation). There is no Holi between October 2026 and March 2027. Windows open 13 days ahead and close 2 days after; many US temples and community groups hold Holi on the nearest weekend, which in 2027 is the weekend after (27-28 Mar), outside the window, so consider extending it to 2027-03-29 if the brief allows.

menus.title: Nowruz Table
menus.intro: Dishes many Persian, Afghan, Kurdish and Central Asian families make to welcome the new year at the spring equinox, heavy on fresh green herbs for the season: herbed rice with fish, kuku sabzi, noodle rice and ash reshteh, with chickpea-flour cookies for guests. Every region and household sets its own table, so treat this as a starting point.

recipeDetails.title: Sabzi Polo ba Mahi (Herbed Rice with Fish)
recipeDetails.summary: Basmati steamed with heaps of parsley, cilantro, dill and chives over a crisp tahdig, served with golden pan-fried white fish and citrus wedges. Many families make it for the first meal of the year.

ingredients.name: Basmati rice
ingredients.note: long-grain, aged if you can find it

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.note: divided: 2 tbsp for the rice water, the rest for the fish

ingredients.name: Parsley
ingredients.note: flat-leaf, leaves and tender stems, finely chopped

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.note: leaves and tender stems, finely chopped

ingredients.name: Chives
ingredients.note: finely chopped, or the green parts of 8 green onions

ingredients.name: Dried fenugreek leaves
ingredients.note: shanbalileh or kasuri methi, from Persian or Indian grocers; leave out if you can't find it

ingredients.name: Saffron threads
ingredients.note: ground with a pinch of sugar and steeped in 3 tbsp hot water; or 1/4 tsp ground turmeric for color

ingredients.name: Vegetable oil
ingredients.note: divided: 1/3 cup for the rice, the rest for frying

ingredients.name: White fish fillets
ingredients.note: cod, halibut, rockfish or tilapia, skin off, cut into 6 pieces; salmon also works

ingredients.name: Seville orange
ingredients.note: narenj, cut into wedges; or 1 lemon and 1 navel orange

instructions: Rinse the rice in several changes of cold water until it runs almost clear. Cover with cold water and 1 tbsp of the salt and soak 30 minutes while you chop the herbs.
Wash the herbs and dry them very well (a salad spinner helps), then chop finely. Toss the parsley, cilantro, dill, chives, fenugreek and garlic together in a bowl.

Bring a large pot of water to a boil with 1 tbsp salt. Drain the rice, add it to the boiling water and cook 5 to 7 minutes, stirring gently once or twice, until the grains are soft outside but still have a firm bite in the middle. Drain in a fine colander and rinse briefly with lukewarm water.

Wipe out the pot, add 3 tbsp of the oil and 2 tbsp water and set over medium heat. Spoon in a thin layer of rice and press it flat for the tahdig. Then layer the rest of the rice with the herbs, a few spoonfuls at a time, mounding it into a cone toward the center.

Poke 5 or 6 holes down to the bottom with the handle of a wooden spoon. Drizzle the rest of the 1/3 cup oil and 1/4 cup water over the top. Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel, cover tightly and cook 10 minutes on medium until you hear sizzling, then turn to low and steam 50 to 60 minutes.
About 20 minutes before the rice is done, pat the fish dry and season with 2 tsp salt and the pepper. Mix the flour with the turmeric on a plate and dredge each piece, shaking off the extra.
Heat the remaining oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the fish in batches 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and it flakes easily with a fork. Drain on paper towels.

Mix a big spoonful of rice into the saffron water. Spoon the rice onto a platter, scatter the saffron rice on top, then loosen the tahdig with a spatula and serve it in pieces on the side. Serve the fish with the citrus wedges to squeeze over.

recipeDetails.title: Reshteh Polo (Persian Noodle Rice with Dates and Raisins)
recipeDetails.summary: Basmati steamed with toasted noodles and topped with golden onions, raisins, dates and cinnamon. Many families make it in the new-year days to 'take hold of the reins' of the year ahead.

ingredients.name: Basmati rice
ingredients.note: rinsed until the water runs almost clear

ingredients.name: Reshteh polo noodles
ingredients.note: toasted Persian noodles from Persian grocers; or linguine broken into 2-inch pieces and toasted in a dry skillet until golden

ingredients.name: Butter
ingredients.note: divided; or more oil to keep it dairy-free

ingredients.name: Advieh
ingredients.note: Persian rice spice mix from Persian grocers; or a pinch each of ground cardamom and cumin

ingredients.name: Saffron threads
ingredients.note: ground with a pinch of sugar and steeped in 3 tbsp hot water

instructions: Cover the rinsed rice with cold water and soak 20 minutes. Meanwhile fry the onions in 2 tbsp of the oil in a skillet over medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden. Set aside.

Bring a large pot of water to a boil with the salt. Add the noodles and cook 3 minutes. Drain the rice and add it to the same pot; boil 5 to 6 minutes more, until the rice is soft outside but firm in the middle. Drain in a fine colander and rinse briefly with lukewarm water.

Wipe out the pot. Add the remaining 2 tbsp oil, 1 tbsp of the butter and 2 tbsp water and set over medium heat. Spoon in the rice and noodles in layers, sprinkling a little cinnamon and the advieh between layers, and mound it toward the center.

Poke a few holes to the bottom with the handle of a wooden spoon, dot with 1 tbsp butter and drizzle with 1/4 cup water. Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel, cover tightly and cook 10 minutes on medium, then turn to low and steam 40 to 45 minutes.

Just before serving, melt the remaining 2 tbsp butter in the onion skillet over medium-low heat. Add the raisins and dates and stir 2 to 3 minutes until the raisins plump, then stir the onions back in with the rest of the cinnamon.

Mix a spoonful of rice into the saffron water. Spoon the rice onto a platter, top with the saffron rice and the onion, date and raisin mixture, and serve the crust from the bottom of the pot on the side.

recipeDetails.title: Nan-e Nokhodchi (Persian Chickpea Flour Cookies)
recipeDetails.summary: Small clover-shaped cookies of toasted chickpea flour, powdered sugar, cardamom and rosewater, topped with pistachio. They melt in the mouth, keep for weeks and wait on many tables for new-year guests.

ingredients.name: Chickpea flour
ingredients.note: roasted chickpea flour from Persian grocers is best; plain chickpea (garbanzo bean) flour works if you toast it first

ingredients.name: Vegetable oil
ingredients.note: neutral, or melted ghee for a richer cookie

ingredients.name: Rosewater
ingredients.note: from Middle Eastern grocers or the international aisle; or 1 tsp vanilla extract

instructions: If your chickpea flour isn't roasted, toast it in a dry skillet over low heat 8 to 10 minutes, stirring constantly, until it smells nutty and darkens a shade. Let it cool completely.
Sift the chickpea flour, powdered sugar and cardamom together into a large bowl.
Add the oil and rosewater and knead with your hand for 5 minutes, until it comes together into a soft, smooth dough that holds when squeezed. If it's crumbly, add oil a teaspoon at a time.
Wrap the dough and chill at least 1 hour, or overnight, so it firms up and is easier to cut.

Heat the oven to 300°F and line two baking sheets with parchment. Pat or roll the dough between two sheets of parchment to about 1/2 inch thick. Cut with a small clover or round cutter, about 1 1/4 inches, and set 1 inch apart. Press a pinch of pistachio into the center of each.
Bake one sheet at a time for 20 to 25 minutes, until the bottoms are just set; the tops should stay pale. They will be very fragile while warm.
Let the cookies cool completely on the sheet before moving them. Keep in an airtight tin at room temperature for up to 3 weeks.

menus.reviewNotes: Sabzi polo ba mahi is the dish most Iranian families associate with the first meal of the new year; the fish is often smoked whitefish (mahi doodi) or Caspian white fish, so I used widely available white fillets and mentioned salmon, and gave a lemon-plus-orange substitute for Seville orange. Kuku sabzi and ash reshteh come from the existing around-the-world pack and genuinely belong (ash reshteh is cooked before the new year and on Sizdah Bedar). Reshteh polo is eaten by many families on the eve or first days of the year; some add lamb or chicken, I kept it a vegetarian side so the fish stays the main. Nan-e nokhodchi stands in for the many Nowruz sweets (nan-e berenji, baklava, sohan, Afghan haft mewa and sabzi challow with chicken are other choices). I left out the haft-sin itself (not a recipe) and dishes specific to other communities rather than guessing. Date: Nowruz falls on 20 or 21 March each year, set by the equinox, so I used a yearly window 03-08 to 03-23 (about 12 days before, two days after); families keep celebrating to Sizdah Bedar on the 13th day, which this window doesn't cover. No web search was used for the date because it doesn't move by more than a day.

menus.title: Easter Dinner
menus.intro: Dishes many American families make for Easter dinner or brunch: a glazed ham, creamy scalloped potatoes, spring asparagus, deviled eggs, hot cross buns and carrot cake. Plenty of tables serve roast lamb instead, and every family has its own must-haves.

recipeDetails.title: Brown Sugar and Honey Glazed Ham
recipeDetails.summary: A fully cooked spiral-sliced ham warmed low and slow under foil, then finished with a sticky brown sugar, honey and Dijon glaze. Feeds a crowd, with leftovers.

ingredients.name: Spiral-sliced ham
ingredients.note: bone-in half ham labeled fully cooked; a 4 to 5 lb boneless ham works, cut the time by about a third

instructions: Take the ham out of the fridge 1 hour ahead. Heat the oven to 325°F and set a rack in the lower third. Throw away any glaze packet if you're making your own.
Set the ham cut side down in a roasting pan, pour the water around it and cover the pan tightly with foil so the slices don't dry out.
Bake about 12 to 14 minutes per pound (1 hour 40 minutes to 1 hour 50 minutes for 8 lb), until a thermometer in the thickest part away from the bone reads 120°F.
Meanwhile simmer the brown sugar, honey, mustard, orange juice, cloves and pepper in a small saucepan for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until syrupy.
Take off the foil and turn the oven up to 400°F. Brush half the glaze over the ham, letting some run between the slices, and bake 10 minutes.
Brush on the rest of the glaze and bake 5 to 10 minutes more, until bubbling and lightly browned at the edges and the ham reads 140°F. Watch it closely; sugar burns fast.
Rest 15 minutes, then cut along the bone to free the slices. Spoon the pan juices over. Save the bone for bean or split pea soup.

recipeDetails.title: Lemon Roasted Asparagus
recipeDetails.summary: Spring asparagus roasted hot and fast with olive oil, then finished with lemon zest and juice. Ready in about 20 minutes and fits in the oven after the ham comes out.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.note: flaky salt if you have it

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Pat the asparagus dry so it roasts rather than steams.
Toss it on a sheet pan with the olive oil, salt, pepper and garlic, if using, and spread it in one layer.
Roast 8 to 12 minutes, depending on thickness, until bright green, just tender and browned in spots.
Grate the lemon zest straight over the hot asparagus, squeeze over half the lemon and scatter the Parmesan, if using. Taste and add more lemon or salt.

recipeDetails.title: Classic Deviled Eggs
recipeDetails.summary: Tangy, creamy deviled eggs with mayo, mustard and a dusting of paprika. A good use for dyed Easter eggs, and easy to make the day before.
instructions: Put the eggs in a pot in one layer, cover with cold water by an inch and bring to a boil. Turn off the heat, cover and leave 12 minutes.
Move the eggs to a bowl of ice water for 10 minutes, then crack and peel them under running water.
Halve each egg lengthwise and pop the yolks into a bowl. Mash the yolks with a fork until fine, then stir in the mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar, salt, pepper and relish, if using, until smooth.
Spoon or pipe the filling into the whites (a zip-top bag with a corner snipped off works well).
Dust with paprika and scatter chives, if using. Chill until serving, up to 1 day ahead, covered loosely.

recipeDetails.title: Spiced Hot Cross Buns
recipeDetails.summary: Soft, lightly sweet yeast buns with cinnamon, orange zest and raisins, piped with a flour-paste cross and brushed with warm jam. Most of the time is rising.

ingredients.name: All-purpose flour
ingredients.note: plus more for kneading; bread flour works too

ingredients.name: Instant yeast
ingredients.note: 2 1/4 tsp; active dry works, proof it in the milk first

ingredients.name: Raisins
ingredients.note: or currants, or a mix with candied peel

instructions: Whisk the 4 cups flour, sugar, yeast, salt, cinnamon, allspice and nutmeg in a large bowl. Add the warm milk, melted butter, egg and orange zest and stir into a shaggy dough.
Knead 8 to 10 minutes by hand (or 6 minutes in a stand mixer with the dough hook) until smooth and springy. Knead in the raisins at the end.
Cover and let rise somewhere warm for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, until doubled.
Divide into 12 equal pieces, roll each into a tight ball and set them barely touching in a parchment-lined 9x13-inch pan. Cover and rise 40 to 50 minutes, until puffy. Heat the oven to 375°F.
Stir the 1/2 cup flour with the water a tablespoon at a time into a thick, pipeable paste. Spoon it into a zip-top bag, snip a corner and pipe a line down each row of buns, then across.
Bake 20 to 22 minutes, until deep golden and the center bun reads about 190°F.
Warm the jam with a teaspoon of water and brush it over the hot buns. Serve warm or split and toasted with butter. They freeze well for up to a month.

recipeDetails.title: Carrot Sheet Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting
recipeDetails.summary: A moist, warmly spiced carrot cake baked in one 9x13 pan and spread with tangy cream cheese frosting. Nuts, raisins and pineapple are up to your family.

ingredients.name: Vanilla extract
ingredients.note: 2 for the cake, 1 for the frosting

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.note: peeled and finely grated, about 3 cups

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 9x13-inch pan and line the bottom with parchment.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, cinnamon and nutmeg in a bowl.
In a large bowl whisk the eggs, oil, both sugars and 2 tsp vanilla until smooth. Stir in the dry ingredients until just combined, then fold in the carrots and any walnuts, raisins or pineapple.
Spread in the pan and bake 35 to 45 minutes, until the top springs back and a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Cool completely in the pan, about 2 hours.
Beat the cream cheese and butter until smooth and fluffy. Beat in the powdered sugar a cup at a time, then the last 1 tsp vanilla.
Spread the frosting over the cooled cake. Keep it in the fridge, and take it out 20 minutes before serving. It's even better made the day before.

menus.reviewNotes: Built as a mainstream American Easter table (ham, scalloped potatoes, asparagus, deviled eggs, carrot cake), which is what most US households I know serve; reviewed as a second cook, the ham method (low under foil, glaze only at the end to 140°F) and scalloped-vs-au-gratin distinction (cheese optional) are right, and nuts/raisins/pineapple in carrot cake and relish in deviled eggs are the classic family arguments, so they're optional. Hot cross buns are traditionally a Good Friday bake in British and Irish families; I kept them as a brunch bread/side and tagged them British & Irish. Left out: roast leg of lamb (the main for many Greek, Italian, British and Middle Eastern Christian families; the intro names it, and it would make a good second main if you want 7 recipes), Italian pastiera and Easter bread, Polish święconka foods, Greek tsoureki and magiritsa, and a green bean casserole or deviled-egg-potato-salad, to keep the menu at 6. No library or pack recipe genuinely fit (closest was simple mashed potatoes), so all 6 are new. No food rules apply beyond the ham being pork; no religious claims made. Dates: Western Easter is 2027-03-28 and 2028-04-16 (2026's, April 5, is before October 2026). Checked with python-dateutil's easter() and independently with the Anonymous Gregorian (Meeus/Jones/Butcher) computus; both agree. Windows open 13 days before and close the day after. Orthodox Easter often falls on a different date (2027-05-02 per dateutil EASTER_ORTHODOX), though in 2028 both fall on April 16; Orthodox families' Pascha tables (lamb, red eggs, tsoureki, paskha/kulich) would deserve their own menu rather than this one.

menus.title: A Passover Seder
menus.intro: Dishes many Ashkenazi families make for the seder: matzo ball soup, a slow-braised brisket, potato kugel, tzimmes, apple-walnut charoset and a flourless chocolate cake. Everything is leaven-free and keeps meat and dairy apart, and recipes vary a lot from family to family.

recipeDetails.title: Passover Braised Brisket with Onions
recipeDetails.summary: Beef brisket braised low and slow on a deep bed of onions with tomato and red wine. It's best made a day ahead, sliced cold and reheated in its gravy.

ingredients.name: Beef brisket
ingredients.note: first cut (flat), fat trimmed to about 1/4 inch

ingredients.name: Tomato paste
ingredients.note: look for a Kosher for Passover label

ingredients.name: Dry red wine
ingredients.note: Kosher for Passover; or more broth with 1 tbsp red wine vinegar

ingredients.name: Beef broth
ingredients.note: Kosher for Passover, or chicken broth

instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F. Pat the brisket dry and season all over with the salt, pepper and paprika.
Heat the oil in a large roasting pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the brisket well on both sides, about 5 minutes a side, then set it on a plate. If it won't fit whole, cut it in half.
Lower the heat to medium, add the onions and a pinch of salt and cook, scraping up the browned bits, until soft and golden, 12 to 15 minutes. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes, then add the broth and bay leaves. Set the brisket on the onions fat side up, tuck the carrots around it and spoon some onions over the top.
Cover tightly with a lid or two layers of foil and braise 3 1/2 to 4 hours, until a fork slides in with almost no resistance.
For the cleanest slices, cool the brisket in its liquid and refrigerate overnight. Lift off the hardened fat, slice the cold meat thinly across the grain, and lay the slices back in the gravy.
Reheat covered at 325°F for 30 to 40 minutes until hot through. Serve with the onions, carrots and plenty of gravy.

recipeDetails.title: Matzo Ball Soup with Homemade Chicken Broth
recipeDetails.summary: Golden chicken soup with carrots, dill and soft matzo balls. Make the broth up to three days ahead and cook the matzo balls in salted water so the soup stays clear.

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs
ingredients.note: bone-in, skin on, or a cut-up whole chicken

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.note: peeled; 2 in chunks for the pot, 3 sliced for serving

ingredients.name: Parsnip
ingredients.note: peeled, in chunks; or another carrot

ingredients.name: Matzo meal
ingredients.note: not cake meal; a box of matzo ball mix also works

ingredients.name: Schmaltz
ingredients.note: melted chicken fat, skimmed from the broth or bought; or vegetable oil

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.note: kosher salt, plus more for the matzo ball water

instructions: Put the chicken in a large stockpot with the water and bring to a simmer, skimming off the foam. Add the onion, chunked carrots, celery, parsnip, half the dill, the parsley and 2 tsp salt.

Simmer gently, uncovered, for 2 1/2 hours; don't let it boil hard or the broth turns cloudy. Strain, keep the chicken meat for the soup or another meal, and skim the fat (save it for the matzo balls).
While the broth simmers, whisk the eggs, schmaltz, seltzer, 1 tsp salt and the pepper. Stir in the matzo meal, cover and chill at least 30 minutes so it can firm up.
Bring a wide pot of well-salted water to a boil. With wet hands, roll the mixture gently into 1-inch balls (about 16); don't pack them tight or they'll be dense.
Drop the balls into the water, turn it down to a steady simmer, cover and cook 30 to 35 minutes without lifting the lid. They'll float and roughly double in size.
Bring the strained broth back to a simmer with the sliced carrots and cook until tender, about 10 minutes. Season with salt.
Add the matzo balls to the broth for a few minutes to warm through. Ladle into bowls with a couple of matzo balls each, some chicken if you like, and chopped dill.

recipeDetails.title: Crispy Potato Kugel
recipeDetails.summary: Grated potatoes and onion baked with eggs and oil in a hot pan until the edges are deep brown and crunchy and the middle is tender. Pareve, so it goes with the brisket.

ingredients.name: Matzo meal
ingredients.note: or potato starch, which makes it gluten-free

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Pour 1/4 cup of the oil into a 9x13-inch metal or glass baking pan and set it in the oven to heat.
Grate the potatoes and onion on the large holes of a box grater or with a food processor's grating disc, putting them in a big bowl as you go. The onion keeps the potatoes from turning gray.
Squeeze the grated mixture hard in a clean kitchen towel, a handful at a time, to get out as much liquid as you can, then put it back in a dry bowl.
Stir in the eggs, the rest of the oil, the matzo meal, salt and pepper until even.
Carefully take out the hot pan and spread the potato mixture in it; it should sizzle. Smooth the top and drizzle with a little more oil if you like.
Bake 60 to 70 minutes, until the top is deep golden and the edges are crisp. Rest 10 minutes, then cut into squares. It reheats well, uncovered, at 375°F.

recipeDetails.title: Carrot and Sweet Potato Tzimmes with Prunes
recipeDetails.summary: Carrots and sweet potatoes slowly baked with prunes, orange juice and a little honey until glossy and soft. A sweet side that sits happily next to brisket.

ingredients.name: Pitted prunes
ingredients.note: or dried apricots, or half and half

ingredients.name: Vegetable oil
ingredients.note: or schmaltz if serving with meat

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F. Put the carrots, sweet potatoes and prunes in a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Whisk the orange juice, honey, oil, cinnamon and salt and pour it over the vegetables. Toss to coat.
Cover tightly with foil and bake 45 minutes, until the carrots are nearly tender.
Uncover, stir and bake 25 to 30 minutes more, stirring once, until the vegetables are soft and the juices have cooked down to a glaze. Serve warm; it reheats well.

recipeDetails.title: Apple and Walnut Charoset
recipeDetails.summary: Chopped apples and walnuts with sweet red wine, cinnamon and a little honey. Made for the seder plate, and most families make extra to eat on matzo all week.

ingredients.name: Apples
ingredients.note: firm and sweet-tart, like Gala or Honeycrisp, cored

ingredients.name: Walnuts
ingredients.note: or pecans; leave out for a nut allergy and add more apple

ingredients.name: Sweet red wine
ingredients.note: Kosher for Passover, such as Concord grape wine; or grape juice

instructions: Toast the walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until fragrant. Let them cool, then chop them finely.
Peel the apples or leave the skin on, then chop them very finely by hand or pulse in a food processor until they look like coarse gravel, not mush.
Stir together the apples, walnuts, wine, honey, cinnamon and lemon juice. Taste and add more wine, honey or cinnamon to your liking.
Cover and chill at least an hour so the flavors meld. Spoon some onto the seder plate and serve the rest in a bowl with matzo.

recipeDetails.title: Flourless Chocolate Cake (Pareve)
recipeDetails.summary: A dense, fudgy chocolate cake made with eggs, oil and cocoa and no flour or butter, so it can follow a meat meal. Dust with cocoa and serve with berries.

ingredients.name: Bittersweet chocolate
ingredients.note: pareve (dairy-free) chips or bar, labeled Kosher for Passover

ingredients.name: Vanilla extract
ingredients.note: Kosher for Passover, or leave out

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease an 8- or 9-inch round cake pan with oil, line the bottom with a circle of parchment and grease the paper.
Melt the chocolate with the oil in a heatproof bowl set over a pot of barely simmering water, or in the microwave in 30-second bursts, stirring until smooth.
Whisk in the sugar, then the eggs one at a time, whisking well after each, then the vanilla. Sift in the cocoa and salt and whisk just until no streaks remain.
Scrape into the pan and bake 30 to 35 minutes, until the top has a thin crust and a toothpick in the center comes out with moist crumbs, not wet batter.
Cool in the pan 10 minutes, run a knife around the edge and turn it out onto a plate. Cool completely; it sinks a little and gets fudgier as it sits.
Dust with cocoa and serve with the berries. It keeps covered at room temperature for 2 days, so it's easy to bake before the seder.

menus.reviewNotes: Written from an Ashkenazi American home: this is a Litvak/Polish-style table, so it avoids kitniyot entirely (no rice, legumes or corn), which also keeps it usable for Sephardi guests; Sephardi families would bring dates-based charoset, lamb or rice dishes instead. Whole meal is kept kosher-style as a meat meal: no dairy anywhere (the cake uses oil and pareve chocolate; kugel and tzimmes are pareve), no pork or shellfish, no wheat flour, bread, pasta or breadcrumbs (matzo meal only, and matzo meal is not tagged gluten-free). Notes point to Kosher for Passover labels on wine, broth, tomato paste and chocolate. Second-cook review: families split on fluffy vs. dense matzo balls (seltzer helps fluffy), on brisket sweetness (some add brown sugar, ketchup or onion soup mix; packaged mixes often aren't KFP, so left out), and on whether tzimmes includes meat. I left out the seder plate items, gefilte fish, a green vegetable and macaroons to stay within 6 recipes; no library or pack recipe fit (all non-KFP or kitniyot). Dates: computed 15 Nisan with a Dershowitz-Reingold Hebrew-calendar implementation in Python (also matches my memory of published calendars): first seder evening Wed 21 Apr 2027 (first day 22 Apr) and Mon 10 Apr 2028 (first day 11 Apr). No Passover falls Oct-Dec 2026. Windows open 12 days before the first seder and close after the diaspora second seder.

menus.title: Cinco de Mayo at Home
menus.intro: Cinco de Mayo marks Mexico's 1862 victory at the Battle of Puebla; it is celebrated far more in the US than in Mexico, where it's mostly a Puebla affair. These are dishes many Mexican and Mexican American families cook for a get-together, starting with Puebla's mole, tinga and chalupas.

recipeDetails.title: Pollo en Mole Poblano
