recipeDetails.summary: Tender poached chicken simmered in a dark, glossy mole poblano made the way many home cooks do it: jarred mole paste loosened with the chicken's own broth and a little Mexican chocolate.

ingredients.name: Bone-in chicken thighs
ingredients.note: or a cut-up whole chicken; skin removed if you like

ingredients.name: White onion
ingredients.note: in one piece, for the broth

ingredients.name: Mole poblano paste
ingredients.note: 8.25 oz jar from the Mexican aisle (Doña María is the one most stores carry), or about 1 cup paste from a Mexican market

ingredients.name: Roma tomato
ingredients.note: charred in a dry skillet, optional but it brightens jarred paste

ingredients.name: Mexican chocolate
ingredients.note: about a third of a tablet such as Ibarra or Abuelita; or bittersweet chocolate and a pinch of cinnamon

instructions: Put the chicken, onion, garlic, bay leaves and 1 tsp salt in a large pot, cover with the water and bring to a simmer. Skim any foam, then simmer gently, partly covered, 35 to 40 minutes until the chicken is cooked through. Lift out the chicken and strain the broth; you need about 4 cups.
If using the tomato, blend it smooth with 1 cup of the warm broth.

Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pot over medium-low heat. Add the mole paste and stir and mash it with a wooden spoon for 2 to 3 minutes until it loosens and smells toasty. Keep the heat low; mole scorches easily.
Pour in 1 cup of broth (or the tomato broth) a little at a time, whisking until smooth, then whisk in 2 to 3 more cups until it is like a thick gravy. Add the chocolate.

Simmer on low, stirring often and scraping the bottom, 15 to 20 minutes until it coats the back of a spoon and the color deepens. Taste and season with salt and a little sugar; add more broth if it thickens too much.
Add the chicken and simmer 10 minutes more so it soaks up the sauce. Serve with sesame seeds on top, with red rice and warm corn tortillas. It is even better the next day.

recipeDetails.title: Tinga de Pollo Tostadas
recipeDetails.summary: Shredded chicken stewed with tomato, sweet onion and smoky chipotle, piled on crisp tostadas over refried beans with crema and queso fresco. A Puebla favorite for feeding a crowd.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.note: 2 whole for poaching, 1 for the sauce

ingredients.name: Roma tomatoes
ingredients.note: or a 14.5 oz can fire-roasted tomatoes

ingredients.name: Chipotle peppers in adobo sauce
ingredients.note: plus 1 tbsp of the sauce; use 1 for milder, 3 or 4 for hotter

ingredients.name: Corn tostadas
ingredients.note: store-bought, or corn tortillas baked crisp

ingredients.name: Mexican crema
ingredients.note: or sour cream thinned with a little milk

instructions: Cover the chicken with water in a pot, add 2 garlic cloves and 1 tsp salt, and simmer 15 to 20 minutes until cooked through. Lift out the chicken, keep 1 cup of the broth, and shred the meat with two forks.
Blend the tomatoes, chipotles, 1 tbsp adobo sauce, the remaining garlic clove and the 1 cup broth until smooth.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onions with a pinch of salt, stirring, 8 to 10 minutes until soft and just golden.
Pour in the tomato-chipotle sauce, add the oregano and bay leaf, and simmer 5 minutes until it darkens a little.
Stir in the chicken and simmer 5 to 10 minutes until the sauce clings to the meat but it is still juicy. Taste for salt and heat, and remove the bay leaf.
To serve, spread each tostada with beans, top with tinga and lettuce, then drizzle with crema and scatter queso fresco and avocado over. Build them at the table so they stay crisp.

recipeDetails.title: Chalupas Poblanas
recipeDetails.summary: Puebla's small fried corn tortillas, each spooned with red or green salsa and topped with shredded pork and onion. A favorite snack in Puebla, made at home for parties.

ingredients.name: Serrano peppers
ingredients.note: or 1 jalapeño; for the green salsa

ingredients.name: Chipotle peppers in adobo sauce
ingredients.note: or 1 dried chile morita, soaked; for the red salsa

ingredients.name: White onion
ingredients.note: quarter for the salsas, the rest finely chopped for topping

ingredients.name: Cooked shredded pork
ingredients.note: leftover carnitas or simmered pork shoulder; or shredded chicken

ingredients.name: Small corn tortillas
ingredients.note: the 4- to 5-inch street-taco size, or thick handmade ones

instructions: Put the tomatillos, serranos and tomatoes in a saucepan, cover with water and simmer 8 to 10 minutes until the tomatillos turn olive green and soft.
Green salsa: blend the tomatillos and serranos with 1 garlic clove, a small piece of the onion, the cilantro, 3/4 tsp salt and a splash of the cooking water until fairly smooth.
Red salsa: blend the tomatoes with the chipotle, the other garlic clove, a small piece of onion and 3/4 tsp salt. Simmer each salsa in a small pan for 5 minutes to deepen the flavor.
Warm the pork with a spoonful of salsa so it is moist. Finely chop the rest of the onion.

Heat a tablespoon of lard in a wide skillet or griddle over medium-high heat. Lay in as many tortillas as fit, spoon salsa over each one right away (red on half, green on the rest) and let them fry 2 to 3 minutes until the edges are crisp and the bottoms are golden. Add lard as needed between batches.
Top with pork and chopped onion and serve straight from the pan; people tend to eat them as fast as they come off the skillet.

recipeDetails.title: Arroz Rojo (Mexican Red Rice)
recipeDetails.summary: Fluffy rice toasted golden, then simmered in a blended tomato and onion broth: the rice that goes with mole at many family parties.

ingredients.name: Chicken broth
ingredients.note: or vegetable broth; use a little less if using tomato sauce

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.note: less if your broth is salty

ingredients.name: Frozen peas and carrots
ingredients.note: many families add them, many don't

instructions: Rinse the rice in a strainer until the water runs mostly clear, then shake it as dry as you can.
Blend the tomatoes, onion and garlic until smooth; you should have about 1 cup. Warm the broth.
Heat the oil in a medium pot over medium heat. Add the rice and fry, stirring often, 6 to 8 minutes until the grains turn opaque and golden in spots.
Pour the tomato purée in carefully (it will sputter) and stir for 2 minutes until it thickens and coats the rice. Add the hot broth and salt, plus the peas and carrots, cilantro and serrano if using.

Bring to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 to 20 minutes without lifting the lid. Take it off the heat and let it sit, covered, 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and pull out the cilantro and serrano.

recipeDetails.title: Guacamole de Molcajete
recipeDetails.summary: Chunky guacamole the way many Mexican kitchens make it: onion, chile and cilantro ground to a paste first, then ripe avocado folded in with lime. No garlic, no fuss.

ingredients.name: Serrano pepper
ingredients.note: or jalapeño; seeded for milder, 2 for hotter

instructions: In a molcajete or a sturdy bowl, grind half the onion, the serrano, half the cilantro and the salt into a rough, juicy paste with the pestle or the back of a fork.
Halve and pit the avocados, scoop them in and mash coarsely; leave plenty of chunks.
Fold in the rest of the onion and cilantro, the tomato if using, and the lime juice. Taste and add more salt or lime.
Serve right away in the molcajete with chips, or press plastic wrap onto the surface and chill for up to 2 hours.

recipeDetails.title: Arroz con Leche
recipeDetails.summary: Creamy Mexican rice pudding simmered with a stick of canela and sweetened with condensed milk, served warm or chilled with cinnamon on top.

ingredients.name: Cinnamon stick
ingredients.note: Mexican canela if you can find it; regular cinnamon works

ingredients.name: Orange peel
ingredients.note: one wide strip, or lime peel

ingredients.name: Raisins
ingredients.note: some families wouldn't make it without them, some pick them out

instructions: Rinse the rice. Put it in a heavy pot with the water, cinnamon stick and orange peel and simmer, uncovered, about 15 minutes until the water is nearly gone and the rice is soft.
Stir in the milk and salt and bring back to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat. Cook 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often and scraping the bottom so it doesn't catch, until creamy and thickened.
Stir in the condensed milk and the raisins if using, and simmer 5 minutes more. Take it off the heat, remove the cinnamon stick and peel, and stir in the vanilla.
It thickens as it cools, so stop when it still looks a little loose. Serve warm, or chill it in cups, with ground cinnamon on top.

menus.reviewNotes: Built around Puebla: mole poblano, tinga and chalupas poblanas are what poblano families actually cook for a fiesta, with red rice as mole's usual partner, guacamole, the library's street-corn salad (esquites-style, a fair stand-in), and arroz con leche as the sweet. The mole uses doctored jarred paste because that is honestly how most home cooks in Mexico and the US make it outside of big occasions; a from-scratch mole (20-plus ingredients, several chiles, a day of work) did not fit a home menu, and I left out chiles en nogada because it is an August-September dish. Families vary on whether the mole is chicken or turkey, peas and carrots in the rice, raisins in the arroz con leche, and tomato in the guacamole, so those are optional or noted. I kept the library taco recipes out to avoid a Taco Tuesday repeat, and avoided drinks and costume or sombrero language entirely. Cinco de Mayo is a fixed date (May 5), so a yearly MM-DD window of 04-22 to 05-06 needs no per-year checking.

menus.title: An Eid al-Adha Table
menus.intro: Dishes many Pakistani and Indian-American families cook to share on Eid al-Adha: a slow lamb biryani or korma, seekh kebabs, cool raita and kachumber, and chilled kheer to finish. Arab, Turkish, West African and Indonesian homes set very different tables, and every family's masala is its own.

recipeDetails.title: Lamb Biryani with Saffron and Fried Onions
recipeDetails.summary: A Pakistani-style Eid biryani: bone-in lamb slow-cooked in a spiced yogurt masala, layered with par-boiled basmati, fried onions and mint, then steamed. Medium heat.

ingredients.name: Bone-in lamb shoulder
ingredients.note: cut into 2-inch pieces by the butcher; halal goat (mutton) is traditional too

ingredients.name: Biryani masala
ingredients.note: Shan or National, in South Asian grocers or the international aisle; or 2 1/2 tbsp garam masala plus 1 1/2 tsp Kashmiri chili powder

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.note: divided, plus 3 tbsp for the rice water

ingredients.name: Basmati rice
ingredients.note: rinsed until the water runs clear, then soaked 30 minutes

ingredients.name: Saffron
ingredients.note: crumbled into 3 tbsp warm milk; or 2 drops yellow food coloring

instructions: Mix the lamb with the yogurt, garlic, ginger, biryani masala and 2 tsp salt. Marinate at least 30 minutes, or overnight in the fridge.
Heat the oil in a large (6- to 7-quart) Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Fry the onions, stirring often, 15 to 18 minutes until deep golden brown. Lift out half onto a paper towel for layering.
Add the cardamom, cinnamon and bay leaves to the pot for 30 seconds, then the tomatoes and serranos. Cook 5 minutes until soft. Add the lamb and all its marinade and cook, stirring, 5 minutes.

Pour in 1 cup water, cover and simmer on low 75 to 90 minutes (goat can take up to 2 hours), stirring now and then, until the lamb is tender and the masala is thick, with oil pooling at the edges. Taste and add salt; it should be well seasoned.

About 20 minutes before the lamb is done, bring a big pot of water to a boil with 3 tbsp salt. Drain the rice, boil it 5 to 6 minutes until about 70% cooked and still firm in the center, then drain well.

Scatter half the mint, cilantro and reserved onions over the lamb and sprinkle with the lemon juice. Spread the rice on top in an even layer, then the rest of the herbs and onions. Drizzle with the saffron milk and ghee if using.
Cover the pot tightly with foil, then the lid. Cook on the lowest heat 20 minutes (set the pot on a heat diffuser or an empty skillet if your burner runs hot), until the rice is tender and steaming.
Rest 10 minutes, then scoop from the bottom with a wide spoon so everyone gets lamb, masala and rice. Serve with raita and kachumber.

recipeDetails.title: Lamb Korma with Fried Onion and Yogurt Sauce
recipeDetails.summary: Bone-in lamb braised in a silky yogurt and browned-onion sauce with whole spices, the way many Pakistani and North Indian homes make it for Eid. Rich, mildly hot, better the next day.

ingredients.name: Bone-in lamb shoulder
ingredients.note: cut into 2-inch pieces; halal goat (mutton) works too

ingredients.name: Kashmiri chili powder
ingredients.note: or 1 tsp paprika plus 1/2 tsp cayenne

ingredients.name: Kewra water
ingredients.note: screwpine water from South Asian grocers; or rose water

instructions: Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and fry the onions, stirring often, 15 to 18 minutes until deep golden brown. Lift them out, leaving the oil, and let cool, then blend or crush them with 3 tbsp of the yogurt to a rough paste.

Add the cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaves to the oil for 30 seconds. Add the lamb, garlic, ginger and salt and cook on medium-high, stirring, 8 to 10 minutes until the lamb is browned in spots and the liquid it gives off has cooked away.

Turn the heat to low and stir in the coriander, chili powder and turmeric for 1 minute. Take the pot off the heat and stir in the rest of the yogurt a spoonful at a time so it doesn't split, then cook on medium-low 5 minutes.
Add 1 1/2 cups water, cover and simmer on low 75 to 90 minutes (up to 2 hours for goat), stirring now and then, until the lamb is tender. Add a splash of water if it starts to catch.
Stir in the onion paste and garam masala and simmer uncovered 10 minutes until the sauce is thick and oil glistens on top. Add the kewra water if using, taste for salt and scatter with cilantro.
Serve with naan, sheermal or plain basmati rice. It keeps 3 days in the fridge and tastes even better reheated.

recipeDetails.title: Kheera Podina Raita (Cucumber-Mint Yogurt)
recipeDetails.summary: Cool, cumin-scented yogurt with grated cucumber and mint, the everyday partner to biryani and kebabs. Ten minutes, no cooking.

ingredients.name: Ground cumin
ingredients.note: best toasted: dry-roast 1 tsp cumin seeds and crush them

ingredients.name: Chaat masala
ingredients.note: from South Asian grocers; or a pinch of black pepper

instructions: Grate the cucumber on the large holes of a box grater, then squeeze it firmly in your hands to drop the extra water.
Whisk the yogurt with 2 to 3 tbsp cold water until smooth and pourable, then stir in the cucumber, mint, cumin and salt.
Sprinkle with chaat masala and cilantro if using. Chill until serving; it keeps a day in the fridge, so stir before serving.

recipeDetails.title: Kachumber Salad
recipeDetails.summary: A crunchy chopped salad of tomato, cucumber and red onion with lemon and green chili, to cut through rich biryani and korma.

ingredients.name: Serrano pepper
ingredients.note: seeded and minced; leave it out for kids

ingredients.name: Chaat masala
ingredients.note: from South Asian grocers; or 1/2 tsp ground cumin

instructions: Put the tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, serrano if using, and cilantro in a bowl.
Just before serving, toss with the lemon juice, salt and chaat masala so the vegetables stay crisp.
Taste and add more lemon or salt. Serve right away, next to the biryani and raita.

menus.reviewNotes: Written from a Pakistani/North Indian (Bakra Eid) home kitchen rather than as a pan-Muslim menu; the intro says so and names other traditions. All halal: no pork or alcohol (kewra and rose water are alcohol-free); the reused pack seekh kebabs are beef or lamb, and cooks buy halal meat. Families vary on biryani vs. korma (many make both), on goat vs. lamb, potatoes in biryani, and sheer khurma vs. kheer for dessert; I chose kheer because sheer khurma is more tied to Eid al-Fitr in many homes. Left out kaleji (fried liver, a first-morning Bakra Eid dish in many homes) and nihari/paye as too niche or long for a US weeknight-style app. Dates: Eid al-Adha 2026 (about May 27) is before October 2026, so only 2027 (expected Sun May 16) and 2028 (expected Fri May 5) fall in range; checked by web search (humanappealusa.org, publicholidays.ae, calendardate.com) and consistent with the ~11-day yearly lunar shift. Windows open ~13 days early and close 3 days after the expected date to cover moon-sighting differences of 1-2 days and the multi-day celebration.

menus.title: A Juneteenth Cookout
menus.intro: Juneteenth marks June 19, 1865, when news of freedom finally reached enslaved people in Galveston, Texas, and many families honor it with a cookout shared across generations. Here are dishes many households bring to that table, from barbecue and greens to a red drink and red velvet cake, though every family, and every region, has its own spread.

recipeDetails.title: Oven-to-Grill Barbecue Pork Spare Ribs
recipeDetails.summary: Spare ribs in a brown sugar and paprika rub, baked low and slow in foil, then finished on the grill with barbecue sauce. No smoker needed, and the oven step can be done a day ahead.

ingredients.name: Pork spare ribs
ingredients.note: 2 racks, St. Louis cut if you can find it; baby back ribs work too, see the last step

ingredients.name: Paprika
ingredients.note: smoked paprika gives a smokier taste

ingredients.name: Barbecue sauce
ingredients.note: your family's favorite, homemade or bottled

instructions: Heat the oven to 300°F. Pat the ribs dry. On the bone side, slide a butter knife under the thin membrane at one end, grip it with a paper towel and pull it off.
Mix the brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, pepper and cayenne, if using. Rub it all over both racks.
Set each rack meat side up on a large sheet of heavy-duty foil, sprinkle with 1 tablespoon of the vinegar and wrap tightly. Put both packets on a rimmed baking sheet.
Bake 2 1/2 hours, until a knife slides easily between the bones. (You can stop here: cool, refrigerate in the foil up to 1 day, and give them an extra 5 minutes a side on the grill.)

Heat a grill to medium, about 350°F to 400°F. Unwrap the ribs and grill them bone side down for 5 minutes, then brush with sauce and grill 10 to 15 minutes more, turning and brushing every few minutes, until sticky and lightly charred. Watch closely: the sugar burns fast. No grill? Broil on the baking sheet 6 inches from the heat, 3 to 4 minutes a side.
Rest 5 minutes, cut between the bones and serve with the rest of the sauce. Baby back ribs need only about 2 hours in the oven.

recipeDetails.title: Hibiscus-Ginger Red Drink
recipeDetails.summary: A deep ruby, sweet-tart pitcher drink of hibiscus steeped with fresh ginger, a homemade take on the red drink at so many Juneteenth tables. Many trace that tradition back to the hibiscus and kola drinks of West Africa.

ingredients.name: Dried hibiscus flowers
ingredients.note: sold as flor de jamaica in the Latin aisle; or 12 hibiscus tea bags

instructions: Rinse the hibiscus in a strainer. Put it in a large pot with 4 cups of the water, the ginger and the cinnamon stick, if using.
Bring to a boil, then turn off the heat and stir in the sugar until it dissolves. Cover and steep 20 to 30 minutes; longer makes it more tart.
Strain into a large pitcher, pressing on the flowers. Stir in the remaining 6 cups of cold water and the lime juice. Taste and add sugar if you like it sweeter.
Chill at least 2 hours, or up to 3 days. Serve over ice with sliced strawberries. It stains, so keep it away from white tablecloths.

recipeDetails.title: Red Velvet Sheet Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting
recipeDetails.summary: A tender, buttermilk-and-cocoa red velvet cake baked in one 9x13 pan and spread with tangy cream cheese frosting. Easy to carry to a cookout and cut into squares for a crowd.

ingredients.name: Buttermilk
ingredients.note: room temperature; or 1 cup milk plus 1 tbsp lemon juice, left 5 minutes

ingredients.name: Red food coloring
ingredients.note: liquid, or 1 tsp gel; beet-based coloring works but bakes up more brownish

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 9x13-inch pan and line the bottom with parchment.
Whisk the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the oil, buttermilk, eggs, food coloring, 1 teaspoon of the vanilla and the vinegar until smooth.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and stir just until no streaks of flour remain. Scrape into the pan and smooth the top.
Bake 28 to 34 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out with a few moist crumbs. Cool completely in the pan, at least 1 hour.
For the frosting, beat the cream cheese and butter until smooth, then beat in the powdered sugar a cup at a time and the remaining vanilla. Spread over the cooled cake.
Cut into squares. Keep it chilled until serving, and in a cooler at an outdoor cookout; it keeps covered in the fridge for 4 days.

menus.reviewNotes: Built around the cookout most Juneteenth celebrations share: barbecue, greens, potato salad, cornbread and red foods and drinks (red drink, red velvet, strawberries, watermelon), which many people connect to resilience and to West African hibiscus and kola traditions. Reused the library's Southern & Soul collard greens and skillet cornbread (the brief said cuisine 'southern-soul', but the valid id in Cuisine.swift is 'southern', so new recipes use that). Families vary a lot: brisket and hot links in Texas, where the holiday began, fried chicken or fish elsewhere, mustard vs. plain mayo potato salad, store-bought red soda (Big Red, strawberry soda) instead of hibiscus, strawberry pie or watermelon instead of cake. Left out a separate fried chicken and baked beans/mac and cheese to keep it to 6, and watermelon needs no recipe. No mood tags: ribs technically pass 'hot-day' via the grill tag, but 2.5 hours in the oven didn't feel honest. Dates: fixed holiday on June 19 (federal holiday since 2021), so a yearly window 06-07 to 06-21 opens 12 days ahead and closes 2 days after; no web search needed.

menus.title: Fourth of July Cookout
menus.intro: Dishes many families bring to a Fourth of July cookout: burgers off the grill (or a skillet veggie burger), potato salad, corn, baked beans, slaw and berry shortcakes. Every backyard has its own spin, from Carolina vinegar slaw to a favorite family potato salad.

recipeDetails.title: Backyard Grilled Cheeseburgers
recipeDetails.summary: Thick, juicy cookout cheeseburgers seasoned simply with salt and pepper and grilled hot, with a skillet method if you don't have a grill.
instructions: Heat a gas grill to medium-high (about 450°F) or light a full chimney of charcoal and spread the coals once they're ashed over. Scrub and oil the grates.

Divide the cold beef into 8 portions of 6 oz and press each gently into a patty about 3/4 inch thick and a little wider than the buns. Don't knead it. Press a shallow dimple into the center of each so they cook flat.
Season both sides generously with salt and pepper right before they go on the grill.
Grill without pressing or moving them for 4 to 5 minutes, until they release easily, then flip once. Cook 3 to 4 minutes more, until 160°F in the center.
Lay a cheese slice on each patty for the last minute and close the lid to melt it. Butter the buns and toast them cut side down at the edge of the grill for 30 to 60 seconds.
No grill: cook the patties in a hot cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat, 4 minutes a side, covering the pan for the last minute to melt the cheese.
Let everyone build their own with lettuce, tomato, onion, pickles, ketchup and mustard.

recipeDetails.title: Cookout Mustard and Egg Potato Salad
recipeDetails.summary: A creamy, tangy potato salad with chopped egg, celery, pickle relish and mustard, made the morning of the cookout so it can chill.

ingredients.name: Yukon Gold potatoes
ingredients.note: or red potatoes, cut in 3/4-inch chunks

instructions: Put the potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water by an inch and add 1 tsp salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer 10 to 12 minutes, until a fork slides in easily but they still hold their shape.
Drain well, spread on a sheet pan and sprinkle with the vinegar while hot. Let them cool to warm, about 15 minutes.
Peel and chop the hard-boiled eggs.
In a large bowl stir together the mayonnaise, mustard, relish, remaining salt and the pepper.
Fold in the potatoes, eggs, celery and onion gently so the potatoes don't turn to mash. Taste and add salt or a splash of pickle juice.
Cover and chill at least 2 hours. Dust with paprika and dill before serving, and keep it cold outside: back in the fridge after about an hour in the heat.

recipeDetails.title: Grilled Corn on the Cob with Butter
recipeDetails.summary: Sweet summer corn charred on the grill and rolled in salted butter, with a stovetop boil if the grill is full.
instructions: Heat the grill to medium-high. Pull the husks and silk off the corn.
Grill the ears, turning every 2 to 3 minutes, until tender and charred in spots all over, 10 to 12 minutes.
No room on the grill: drop the ears into a big pot of boiling unsalted water and cook 4 to 5 minutes.
Rub each hot ear with butter and sprinkle with salt and pepper. Set out lime wedges and chili powder for anyone who likes them.

recipeDetails.title: Brown Sugar Bacon Baked Beans
recipeDetails.summary: Canned beans baked low and slow with bacon, onion, molasses, brown sugar and mustard until thick and glossy. They hold well on a warm grill.

ingredients.name: Pork and beans
ingredients.note: 28 oz each; or navy beans, drained

instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F. In an ovenproof pot or Dutch oven, cook the bacon over medium heat until it's browned but not crisp, about 6 minutes.
Add the onion and cook in the bacon fat until soft, 5 minutes.
Stir in the beans with their sauce, the ketchup, brown sugar, molasses, mustard, Worcestershire, vinegar and pepper and bring to a simmer.
Bake uncovered for 75 to 90 minutes, stirring once or twice, until thick and dark around the edges.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving. They reheat well, so you can make them a day ahead and warm them in the oven or on the side of the grill.

recipeDetails.title: Red, White and Blue Berry Shortcakes
recipeDetails.summary: Tender buttermilk biscuits split and piled with sugared strawberries, blueberries and whipped cream for a cool, festive cookout dessert.

ingredients.name: Buttermilk
ingredients.note: plus more for brushing; or milk with 2 tsp lemon juice

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with parchment. Toss the strawberries and blueberries with 3 tbsp of the sugar and let them sit while you bake, so they make their own syrup.
Whisk the flour, 3 tbsp sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl. Rub or cut in the cold butter until the biggest pieces are the size of peas.
Stir in the buttermilk just until a shaggy dough forms. Pat it out on a floured counter 1 inch thick and cut 8 rounds or squares, pressing the scraps together once.
Set them on the sheet, brush the tops with buttermilk and sprinkle with 1 tbsp sugar. Bake 13 to 15 minutes, until golden. Cool at least 10 minutes.
Whip the cream with the remaining 1 tbsp sugar and the vanilla to soft peaks.
Split each shortcake, spoon berries and their juice over the bottom, add whipped cream and the top. Keep the cream chilled until serving on a hot day.

menus.reviewNotes: Built as a standard US backyard cookout: hamburgers (salt-and-pepper patties, American cheese, build-your-own toppings), mustard-egg potato salad, grilled corn, bacon-and-brown-sugar baked beans from canned pork and beans, slaw and strawberry-blueberry shortcakes. Second-cook review: tightened the potato salad to chill and food-safety timing, added a skillet method to the burger and a boil method to the corn so the menu works without a grill, and reused the library's skillet Mushroom Black Bean Burgers as the vegetarian main. I reused the library's vinegar slaw rather than writing a creamy one; families split on mayo vs. vinegar slaw, and the intro acknowledges both. Families also vary with hot dogs, bratwurst, BBQ chicken or ribs, deviled eggs, mac salad, watermelon and flag cakes; hot dogs and chicken were left out to keep it to 7 recipes and one grilled main. Baked beans use bacon, so they aren't vegetarian; vegetarian guests can use canned vegetarian beans with smoked paprika. Dates: Independence Day is fixed on July 4, so a yearly window of 06-24 to 07-05 (about 10 days of shopping lead plus the day after) was used; no web check was needed.

menus.title: Chuseok Harvest Table
menus.intro: Dishes many Korean families make when everyone gathers for Chuseok: slow-braised galbi-jjim, japchae, plates of golden jeon, seasoned namul and songpyeon pinched by hand the night before. Every family and region does it a little differently, so make it your own.

recipeDetails.title: Galbi-jjim (Korean Braised Short Ribs)
recipeDetails.summary: Bone-in short ribs braised slowly in soy sauce, Asian pear and garlic with radish, carrot, shiitake and chestnuts until glossy and falling off the bone. The centerpiece of many holiday tables.

ingredients.name: Beef short ribs
ingredients.note: bone-in, English cut (2- to 3-inch chunks), not thin flanken

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.note: regular Korean or Japanese soy sauce; tamari for gluten-free

ingredients.name: Asian pear
ingredients.note: peeled and grated; or 1 Bosc pear or 1/2 cup unsweetened apple juice

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.note: half grated into the sauce, half cut in wedges

ingredients.name: Daikon radish
ingredients.note: Korean radish (mu) if you can find it; peeled, cut in 2-inch chunks with edges rounded off

ingredients.name: Dried shiitake mushrooms
ingredients.note: soaked 30 minutes in warm water, stems removed, halved; or fresh shiitake

ingredients.name: Dried jujubes
ingredients.note: Korean red dates, rinsed; skip if you can't find them

instructions: Soak the short ribs in cold water for 30 minutes to 1 hour, changing the water once, to draw out the blood. Trim off thick outer fat.
Put the ribs in a large pot, cover with fresh water and bring to a boil. Boil 8 minutes, then drain, rinse the ribs and wash the pot. This keeps the braise clean and less greasy.
Stir together the soy sauce, grated pear, grated onion, garlic, ginger, brown sugar, sesame oil and pepper.
Return the ribs to the pot with the sauce and 3 cups water. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 1 hour, turning the ribs now and then.
Add the radish, carrots, shiitake, onion wedges, and the chestnuts and jujubes if using. Simmer covered 40 to 50 minutes more, until the meat pulls easily from the bone and the radish is tender.
Uncover and simmer 5 to 10 minutes, basting, until the sauce thickens and coats the ribs. Skim the fat from the top, taste and add a little soy sauce or sugar if needed.
Pile onto a platter, spoon the sauce over and scatter with green onions and sesame seeds. It tastes even better made a day ahead: chill, lift off the fat, then reheat gently.

recipeDetails.title: Hobak-jeon and Dongtae-jeon (Zucchini and Fish Jeon)
recipeDetails.summary: Two holiday jeon from one setup: zucchini rounds and thin white fish slices dredged in flour, dipped in egg and pan-fried golden, with a soy-vinegar dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Zucchini
ingredients.note: medium, cut in 1/4-inch rounds; Korean zucchini (aehobak) if you have it

ingredients.name: Pollock fillets
ingredients.note: frozen Alaska pollock, thawed and patted dry; or cod or haddock

ingredients.name: All-purpose flour
ingredients.note: for dredging; Korean pancake mix (buchimgaru) also works

ingredients.name: Eggs
ingredients.note: beaten with a pinch of salt

ingredients.name: Vegetable oil
ingredients.note: for pan-frying, added a few tablespoons at a time

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.note: thinly sliced, for garnish; or a few red bell pepper bits

instructions: Lay the zucchini rounds on a towel and sprinkle with 1/2 tsp salt. Cut the fish on an angle into thin slices about 2 inches across and 1/4 inch thick, and season with 1 tsp salt and the pepper. Let both sit 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Stir together the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, sesame seeds and 1 tbsp water for dipping.
Set out three plates in a row: flour, beaten egg, and a sheet pan lined with paper towels.

Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Dredge a zucchini round in flour, tap off the extra, dip it in egg and lay it in the pan. Fill the pan, and press a slice of chili on top of each if you like.
Cook 2 to 3 minutes a side, until the egg is set and lightly golden, not browned. Keep the heat moderate so the egg stays yellow. Move to the paper towels.
Cook the fish slices the same way, 2 to 3 minutes a side, until opaque in the middle. Add oil as needed and wipe out burnt bits between batches.
Arrange the jeon on a platter with the dipping sauce. They are good warm or at room temperature, and you can rewarm them in a dry skillet.

recipeDetails.title: Samsaek Namul (Three-Color Seasoned Vegetables)
recipeDetails.summary: Three simple namul for the holiday table: garlicky spinach, crunchy soybean sprouts and savory sauteed shiitake (or gosari fern), each seasoned lightly with sesame.

ingredients.name: Spinach
ingredients.note: mature bunch spinach, roots trimmed and washed; or 2 bags baby spinach

ingredients.name: Soybean sprouts
ingredients.note: from Asian markets; mung bean sprouts work, boil them only 2 minutes

ingredients.name: Shiitake mushrooms
ingredients.note: fresh, sliced; or 1 lb rehydrated gosari (fernbrake) from a Korean market

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.note: Korean soup soy sauce (guk-ganjang) if you have it; tamari for gluten-free

instructions: Spinach: blanch in a large pot of boiling salted water for 30 seconds, then rinse under cold water and squeeze out as much water as you can. Cut into 3-inch lengths and toss with a third of the garlic and green onions, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tbsp sesame oil and 2 tsp sesame seeds.

Sprouts: pick off any brown tails. Put them in a pot with 1 cup water and 1/4 tsp salt, cover and cook 7 to 8 minutes without lifting the lid, then drain and spread out to cool. Toss with another third of the garlic and green onions, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 2 tsp sesame seeds and salt to taste.

Mushrooms (or gosari): heat the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the mushrooms with the last of the garlic and cook 4 to 5 minutes, until soft. Add the soy sauce and 2 tbsp water and cook until absorbed. For gosari, cook 8 to 10 minutes with the lid on until tender. Finish with the remaining green onions, sesame oil and sesame seeds.
Taste each namul and adjust the salt. Arrange the three side by side on a plate or in separate bowls. They keep 2 to 3 days in the fridge and are served cold or at room temperature.

recipeDetails.title: Songpyeon (Half-Moon Rice Cakes with Sesame-Honey Filling)
recipeDetails.summary: Chewy steamed rice cakes shaped by hand into little half-moons around a crunchy sesame, honey and brown sugar filling. A family project for the night before Chuseok.

ingredients.name: Rice flour
ingredients.note: non-glutinous; Korean frozen wet rice flour (maepssal-garu) is best, or dry Asian rice flour such as Erawan. Not sweet/glutinous rice flour

ingredients.name: Boiling water
ingredients.note: plus more a spoonful at a time; wet rice flour needs less

ingredients.name: Pine needles
ingredients.note: washed, to line the steamer for the traditional scent; parchment works fine

instructions: Filling: grind the sesame seeds roughly in a mortar or spice grinder, leaving some whole. Stir in the brown sugar, a pinch of salt and the honey until it clumps when pressed.

Dough: mix the rice flour and salt in a bowl (if using dry flour, sift it first). Pour in the boiling water a little at a time, stirring with a spoon, then knead with your hands once cool enough. Add more hot water a spoonful at a time until the dough is smooth and soft like play dough and doesn't crack at the edges.
If you want colors, knead the matcha into a third of the dough. Keep all the dough covered with a damp towel or plastic wrap so it doesn't dry out.

Pinch off a walnut-size piece and roll it into a ball. Press your thumb in to make a cup, add about 1/2 tsp filling, then fold it closed and pinch the seam firmly into a half-moon. Squeeze gently in your palm to press out air. Make the rest.

Line a steamer basket with damp cloth or parchment (and the pine needles, if using). Set the songpyeon in a single layer, not touching. Steam over boiling water 20 to 25 minutes, until the dough turns slightly glossy and translucent.
Rinse the cakes quickly in cold water so they don't stick, drain, and brush lightly with sesame oil. Eat the same day; they firm up overnight but soften again after a few minutes of steaming.

menus.reviewNotes: Five dishes a Korean-American family would recognize from a Chuseok spread: galbi-jjim as the main, the library's japchae (sweet potato glass noodles with beef, a good match as written), two classic jeon (hobak-jeon and dongtae-jeon with frozen pollock, cod as the swap), samsaek namul (spinach, soybean sprouts, and shiitake standing in for gosari, which is offered as the authentic option), and songpyeon with the sesame-honey filling, made with non-glutinous rice flour (the recipe warns against sweet rice flour, a common mistake). Families vary: some add toran-guk (taro soup), LA galbi instead of galbi-jjim, more jeon (dongeurang-ttaeng, kkochi-jeon), japchae with pork, songpyeon filled with chestnut or beans, and families who hold charye arrange food for ancestors; I left out charye and religious framing on purpose, and skipped toran-guk because taro and soup soy sauce are harder to find and the menu already has five dishes. Galbi-jjim is kept free of rice wine for simplicity (some families add mirin or cheongju). Mood tags: only cozy-night-in on galbi-jjim (150 min total). Dates: Chuseok is the 15th day of the 8th lunar month; I computed it with the korean-lunar-calendar Python package (KASI-based): 2026-09-25 (before October 2026, so no window), 2027-09-15 and 2028-10-03, matching what I know of the published Korean public holidays (Sept 14-16, 2027; Oct 2-4, 2028). Windows open about 13 days before Chuseok and close 2 days after.

menus.title: Mid-Autumn reunion dinner
menus.intro: Dishes many Chinese, Taiwanese and Vietnamese families gather around under the full moon: duck braised with taro, a silky poached chicken, Taiwanese-style backyard barbecue and pomelo, with plenty of variation from home to home. Most families buy their mooncakes, but these no-bake snow skin ones are a fun project with kids.

recipeDetails.title: Woo Tau Mun Ngap (Cantonese Braised Duck with Taro)
recipeDetails.summary: Duck legs browned in their own fat, then braised with ginger and red fermented bean curd until the taro turns soft and soaks up the savory sauce.

ingredients.name: Duck legs
ingredients.note: about 4 legs; Asian markets and many butcher counters carry them. Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs work too (cut the first simmer to 25 minutes)

ingredients.name: Taro root
ingredients.note: 1 large taro; peel with gloves on, since the raw sap can itch, and cut into 1 1/2-inch chunks. Yukon Gold potatoes can stand in

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.note: white parts in 2-inch lengths, greens sliced for garnish

ingredients.name: Red fermented bean curd
ingredients.note: nam yu, sold in jars at Asian markets; mash with 1 tbsp of its liquid. Or use 1 tbsp hoisin plus 1 tsp white miso

instructions: Pat the duck legs dry and trim off any loose flaps of fat. Lay them skin side down in a cold Dutch oven, then set over medium heat and cook 10 to 12 minutes, until the skin is deep golden and plenty of fat has melted out. Turn and brown the other side 2 minutes, then move the duck to a plate.

Pour off all but about 2 tablespoons of the fat (save the rest for frying rice or potatoes). Add the taro and fry over medium-high, turning, until the edges are lightly golden, about 6 minutes. Set the taro aside.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the ginger, garlic and scallion whites and stir 1 minute, then stir in the mashed fermented bean curd for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return the duck to the pot. Add the Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar and water, and bring to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to low and simmer 60 minutes, turning the legs once.
Skim off the fat that rises to the top. Tuck the taro into the liquid, cover again and simmer 20 to 25 minutes, until a chopstick slides easily through the taro and the duck is tender.
Uncover and simmer a few more minutes if the sauce is thin; the taro will thicken it as it softens. Taste for salt, scatter the scallion greens over and serve with rice.

recipeDetails.title: Kao Rou (Taiwanese Mid-Autumn Barbecue Pork and Corn)
recipeDetails.summary: Thin-sliced pork and sweet corn brushed with a garlicky soy barbecue glaze, grilled fast and tucked into toast with a scallion, the way many Taiwanese families spend the full moon.

ingredients.name: Pork shoulder
ingredients.note: sliced about 1/4 inch thick; Asian markets sell it pre-sliced for barbecue or hot pot. Thin-sliced pork belly or boneless chicken thighs also work

ingredients.name: Rice wine
ingredients.note: Taiwanese mijiu or Shaoxing wine, or dry sherry

ingredients.name: Taiwanese barbecue sauce
ingredients.note: Kimlan or Bull Head brand at Asian markets; it can replace the soy-honey glaze above or be brushed on at the end

ingredients.name: Shacha sauce
ingredients.note: Bull Head brand; a savory brisket-and-shrimp-paste spread many families brush on the corn

instructions: Whisk the soy sauce, honey, garlic, rice wine and five-spice powder. Toss the pork with a third of it and marinate 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to overnight in the fridge. Keep the rest of the glaze for brushing.
Heat a charcoal or gas grill to medium-high, or use a grill pan on the stove (open a window). Oil the grates.
Grill the corn, turning, until charred in spots, 10 to 12 minutes. Brush it with the glaze (or with shacha sauce or bottled barbecue sauce) for the last 2 minutes only, since the sugar burns quickly.
Grill the pork in batches 2 to 3 minutes per side, brushing with glaze after you turn it, until cooked through with dark, sticky edges. Grill the scallions for a minute until soft and striped.
Toast the bread on the cooler edge of the grill, about 30 seconds per side.
Serve everything straight off the grill: fold a slice of pork and a grilled scallion into a piece of toast like a sandwich, with the corn on the side.

recipeDetails.title: Goi Buoi (Vietnamese Pomelo Salad with Shrimp)
recipeDetails.summary: Juicy pomelo segments tossed with shrimp, herbs and a sweet-sour fish sauce dressing, topped with peanuts and crispy shallots.

ingredients.name: Pomelo
ingredients.note: about 3 lb; pick one heavy for its size. Or 2 pink grapefruits, with an extra 1/2 tbsp sugar in the dressing

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.note: leaves, or Vietnamese coriander (rau ram) if you can find it

ingredients.name: Fried shallots
ingredients.note: jarred, from Asian markets; or canned crispy onions

instructions: Score the pomelo's thick skin into quarters and peel it off. Pull the fruit apart into segments, then peel away the tough membrane from each and break the flesh into bite-size pieces. Let them drain in a colander while you prep the rest.
Drop the shrimp into boiling salted water and cook 2 to 3 minutes, until pink and curled. Drain, cool under cold water and slice each in half lengthwise.
Stir the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, garlic and chili until the sugar dissolves.
Just before serving, toss the pomelo, shrimp, carrot, mint and cilantro with most of the dressing. Taste and add the rest if needed.
Pile onto a plate and scatter the peanuts and fried shallots over the top so they stay crunchy.

recipeDetails.title: Snow Skin Mooncakes with Red Bean Filling
recipeDetails.summary: No-bake mooncakes with a soft, chewy steamed rice-flour skin wrapped around sweet red bean paste. A fun make-ahead project with kids.

ingredients.name: Glutinous rice flour
ingredients.note: also sold as sweet rice flour or mochiko, plus 3 tbsp more for dusting

ingredients.name: Cornstarch
ingredients.note: or wheat starch, which is what many bakeries use

ingredients.name: Whole milk
ingredients.note: or coconut milk for a dairy-free version

ingredients.name: Red bean paste
ingredients.note: sweetened, canned or in a pouch at Asian markets; lotus seed paste or black sesame filling work too

instructions: Whisk the glutinous rice flour, rice flour, cornstarch, powdered sugar, milk and oil until smooth. Pour into a shallow heatproof dish.
Steam the dish, covered, over boiling water for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring once halfway, until the batter is set and no wet patches remain. Let it cool until you can handle it.
Meanwhile toast the extra 3 tablespoons of glutinous rice flour in a dry skillet over low heat, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes, until it smells nutty but is still pale. This is your dusting flour.

Wearing food-safe gloves or with lightly oiled hands, knead the warm dough for 3 to 5 minutes until smooth and stretchy. Divide it into 12 pieces, and the red bean paste into 12 balls of about 2 tablespoons each.
Flatten a piece of dough into a thin round, set a ball of filling in the middle and gather the dough up around it, pinching to seal. Roll it smooth.

Dust lightly with the toasted flour and press into a 50 g mooncake mold, tap out onto a tray. No mold? Flatten each ball into a puck and press a pattern on top with a cookie stamp or the back of a fork.
Chill at least 1 hour before eating. Keep them covered in the fridge and eat within 3 days; the skin firms as it chills and softens again after 10 minutes on the counter.

menus.reviewNotes: Written as a home cook, reviewed as a second. Taro duck (woo tau mun ngap) is a Cantonese Mid-Autumn dish, taro and duck both being in season; white-cut chicken is the bird many Cantonese and Vietnamese families (as ga luoc, with salt-pepper-lime instead of ginger-scallion oil) put on any reunion table. Taiwanese barbecue is a modern tradition (since the 1980s, helped by sauce-brand ads) and many families simply grill whatever is on sale; pork, corn, toast and shacha sauce are the common thread. Pomelo is eaten fresh almost everywhere (kids wear the peel as hats in Taiwan; Vietnamese fruit trays carve it), so the salad is an extra way to use it, not a substitute. Families vary a lot: Shanghai and northern households differ from Cantonese ones (osmanthus wine, hairy crab, lotus root), and many Vietnamese homes treat Tet Trung Thu mainly as a children's lantern festival with mooncakes (banh nuong, banh deo) and fruit rather than a big dinner. Left out: baked Cantonese mooncakes (most people buy them; the snow skin recipe is the honest home-friendly option and is not claimed to be Vietnamese banh deo, which uses a different dough), hairy crab (hard to source), and a whole roast duck (usually bought from a BBQ shop). Reused the library blistered garlic green beans as the stir-fried green. No mood tags beyond cozy-night-in on the 125-minute braise. Dates: festival is 15th day of 8th lunar month (calculated calendar, not moon-sighted): 2027-09-15 and 2028-10-03, confirmed via web search (chinahighlights, publicholidays.com.au, chineselunarcalendar.org, days.to). The 2026 festival (Sept 25) has already passed, so only two windows; each opens 13 days before and closes 2 days after.

menus.title: A Sweet New Year Table
menus.intro: Sweet dishes for a sweet year that many Jewish families bring to the Rosh Hashanah table: slow-braised brisket or honey roast chicken, a round challah, tzimmes, pomegranate and a dark honey cake. Every family has its own versions, so keep what's yours and borrow the rest.

recipeDetails.title: Sweet-and-Sour Braised Brisket with Onions
recipeDetails.summary: Beef brisket braised low and slow on a bed of onions with tomato, brown sugar and vinegar until it slices tender. Even better made a day ahead.

ingredients.name: Beef brisket
ingredients.note: first (flat) cut, fat trimmed to about 1/4 inch

ingredients.name: Brown sugar
ingredients.note: packed; some families use honey instead

instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F. Pat the brisket dry and season it all over with the salt, pepper and paprika.
Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy roasting pan over medium-high heat. Brown the brisket well, about 5 minutes per side, then lift it out.
Lower the heat to medium, add the onions and a pinch of salt, and cook, scraping up the browned bits, until soft and golden, about 12 minutes. Stir in the garlic for a minute.
Whisk the tomato sauce, broth, brown sugar and vinegar together. Set the brisket fat side up on the onions, pour the sauce over, and tuck the carrots and bay leaves around it.
Cover tightly with a lid or foil and braise 3 to 3 1/2 hours, until a fork slides in with almost no resistance. Check once or twice and add a splash of water if it looks dry.

For the cleanest slices, cool it, refrigerate overnight in its sauce, then skim the fat, slice thinly across the grain and rewarm covered at 325°F for 30 to 40 minutes. To serve the same day, rest it 20 minutes before slicing.
Fish out the bay leaves and spoon the onions, carrots and sauce over the slices.

recipeDetails.title: Honey Roast Chicken with Apples and Onions
recipeDetails.summary: Chicken thighs and drumsticks roasted over apples and onions with a honey-mustard glaze. A lighter, faster main for a smaller holiday table, or alongside brisket.

ingredients.name: Apple
ingredients.note: firm, like Honeycrisp or Gala, cut in wedges

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Spread the apples and onions on a large rimmed sheet pan and toss with 1 tablespoon of the oil and a pinch of salt.
Pat the chicken dry, rub it with the remaining oil, salt, pepper and thyme, and set it skin side up on top of the apples and onions.
Roast 25 minutes. Meanwhile, stir the honey, mustard and garlic together.
Brush the honey glaze over the chicken and roast 20 to 25 minutes more, until the skin is deep golden and the thickest thigh reads 175°F.
Rest 5 minutes, then pile the chicken on a platter with the soft apples and onions and the pan juices. Scatter pomegranate seeds over if you like.

recipeDetails.title: Round Raisin Challah
recipeDetails.summary: A soft, honey-sweetened egg bread coiled into a round loaf, with or without raisins. Made with oil, not butter, so it goes with a meat meal.

ingredients.name: All-purpose flour
ingredients.note: plus more for kneading; bread flour works too

instructions: Whisk the yeast into the warm water with a teaspoon of the honey and let it foam, about 5 minutes. Soak the raisins in hot water if using.
Whisk in the rest of the honey, the oil and 2 of the eggs. Add the flour and salt and stir into a shaggy dough.
Knead on a lightly floured counter 8 to 10 minutes (or 6 minutes in a stand mixer with the dough hook) until smooth and only a little tacky. Knead in the drained raisins.
Put the dough in an oiled bowl, cover, and let it rise in a warm spot until doubled, 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Roll the dough into one rope about 30 inches long, thicker at one end. Coil it into a spiral starting from the thick end and tuck the thin end underneath. Set it on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Cover loosely and let it rise again until puffy, 45 minutes to an hour. Heat the oven to 350°F.
Beat the last egg with a splash of water, brush it over the loaf, and sprinkle with sesame seeds if you like.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes, until deep golden and it sounds hollow when tapped underneath; tent with foil if it browns too fast. Cool on a rack before slicing.

recipeDetails.title: Carrot and Sweet Potato Tzimmes
recipeDetails.summary: Carrots, sweet potatoes and prunes baked slowly in orange juice and honey until glossy and soft. A sweet side for a sweet year.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and oil a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Whisk the orange juice, honey, oil, lemon juice, cinnamon and salt together in a large bowl.
Add the carrots, sweet potatoes and prunes and toss to coat, then spread them in the dish and pour any liquid left in the bowl over the top.
Cover tightly with foil and bake 45 minutes, until the carrots are just tender.
Uncover, stir, and bake 25 to 30 minutes more, stirring once, until the liquid has cooked down to a glossy glaze. Serve warm; it reheats well.

recipeDetails.title: Pomegranate, Apple and Herb Salad
recipeDetails.summary: Crisp apple, pomegranate seeds and toasted walnuts over greens and fresh herbs, with a honey-lemon dressing. A bright, crunchy plate next to the braised dishes.

ingredients.name: Pomegranate seeds
ingredients.note: from 1 pomegranate, or a container of arils

instructions: Toast the walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat, shaking the pan, until fragrant, 4 to 5 minutes. Let them cool.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, honey, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Slice the apples just before serving and toss them in the dressing so they don't brown.
Add the greens, parsley and mint and toss gently. Scatter the pomegranate seeds and walnuts over the top and serve right away.

recipeDetails.title: Spiced Honey Cake (Lekach)
recipeDetails.summary: A moist, dark honey cake spiced with cinnamon and ginger and made with oil and coffee, so it is dairy-free. It slices best a day after baking.

ingredients.name: Brewed coffee
ingredients.note: warm, regular or decaf; strong black tea works too

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 9x13-inch pan (or two 9x5-inch loaf pans) and line the bottom with parchment.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, ginger, cloves and salt in a bowl.
In a large bowl, whisk the honey, brown sugar, oil and eggs until smooth, then whisk in the warm coffee and orange juice.
Add the dry ingredients and whisk just until no dry streaks remain; the batter will be thin. Pour it into the pan and scatter the almonds over if using.
Bake 45 to 55 minutes (55 to 65 for loaves), until the top springs back and a skewer comes out clean. Honey cakes brown fast, so tent with foil after 30 minutes if the top darkens.
Cool completely in the pan, then wrap well and leave it overnight at room temperature for the best flavor and texture before slicing.

menus.reviewNotes: Second-cook review: this is an Ashkenazi-American table (brisket, round challah, tzimmes, lekach), which is what most US households will recognize; the pomegranate salad nods to Israeli and Sephardi tables, where pomegranate is one of the simanim. Everything is kosher-style and pareve or meat: no pork, no shellfish, no dairy anywhere (challah and honey cake use oil; coffee in the cake is black), so it all works in one meat meal. Families vary a lot: brisket sweet-and-sour vs. onion-soup-mix vs. wine-braised (I avoided wine and soup mix to keep it simple and widely kosher-available); tzimmes with or without meat or prunes; challah plain or with raisins. Left out: apples dipped in honey (not a recipe, mentioned in spirit), gefilte fish and chicken soup with kneidlach (good but would push past 6 dishes), and the Sephardi seder of simanim (leeks, beets, dates, fish head), which deserves its own menu rather than a token gesture. Intro makes no religious claims beyond 'sweet year'. Dates: Rosh Hashanah 5787 was Sept 11-13, 2026, before the October 2026 start, so it is excluded. 5788 begins at sundown Fri Oct 1, 2027 (days Oct 2-3); 5789 begins at sundown Wed Sept 20, 2028 (days Sept 21-22). Checked by web search against Hebcal and Chabad.org listings, matching my own calendar knowledge. Windows open ~12 days before the eve and close a day after the second day.

menus.title: Día de Muertos
menus.intro: On November 1 and 2, many families set an ofrenda and cook the foods their loved ones enjoyed, gathering to remember them with stories and a full table. These are dishes many families make for these days, from tamales and mole to pan de muerto and champurrado, and every region and household has its own versions.

recipeDetails.title: Mole Poblano with Chicken
recipeDetails.summary: Chicken simmered in a dark, glossy mole of toasted dried chiles, nuts, sesame, raisins and Mexican chocolate. A labor of love that tastes even better the next day.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.note: for poaching the chicken; this becomes your broth

ingredients.name: White onion
ingredients.note: half for the broth, half roughly chopped for the mole

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.note: 2 for the broth, 3 peeled for the mole

ingredients.name: Dried pasilla chiles
ingredients.note: stemmed and seeded; in the Latin aisle, or use 2 more anchos

ingredients.name: Dried mulato chiles
ingredients.note: stemmed and seeded; or use 2 more anchos

ingredients.name: Sesame seeds
ingredients.note: plus more to scatter on top

ingredients.name: Mexican chocolate
ingredients.note: such as Ibarra or Abuelita; or 1 oz semisweet chocolate plus a pinch more cinnamon

ingredients.name: Ground cinnamon
ingredients.note: Mexican canela if you have it

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: or a little grated piloncillo; to taste

instructions: Put the chicken in a large pot with the water, half the onion, 2 garlic cloves and 1 tsp salt. Bring to a simmer, skim, and cook gently 35 minutes until tender. Lift out the chicken and keep the broth.

Meanwhile, toast the chiles a few at a time in a dry skillet over medium heat, about 10 seconds per side, just until fragrant; if they smoke or blacken, the mole turns bitter. Cover with hot water and soak 20 minutes, then drain.

In the same skillet, char the tomatoes all over, about 8 minutes. Add 2 tbsp oil and fry the almonds until golden, then the sesame seeds for a minute, then the raisins until they puff. Scoop it all into the blender.
Fry the torn tortilla in the oil left in the pan until crisp, then the chopped onion and 3 garlic cloves until soft and browned. Add to the blender.
Add the drained chiles, tomatoes, cinnamon, cloves, black pepper and 2 cups of the chicken broth. Blend until very smooth, in batches if needed. For a silkier mole, push it through a sieve.
Heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Pour in the paste (it will splatter; keep a lid handy) and fry, stirring, 8 to 10 minutes until it darkens and thickens.

Stir in the chocolate, sugar and 3 cups broth. Simmer on low, uncovered, 30 to 40 minutes, stirring often so it doesn't catch, until it coats a spoon. Add more broth if it gets too thick, and season with salt and sugar.

Nestle the chicken in the mole and warm through, about 10 minutes. Scatter with sesame seeds and serve with red rice and warm corn tortillas. Short on time? Many cooks start from a jar of mole paste thinned with this broth.

recipeDetails.title: Red Chile Pork Tamales
recipeDetails.summary: Tender pork in guajillo chile sauce wrapped in fluffy masa and steamed in corn husks. Makes about two dozen, best made together with family and great frozen.

ingredients.name: Dried guajillo chiles
ingredients.note: stemmed and seeded; in the Latin aisle

ingredients.name: Masa harina
ingredients.note: instant corn masa flour for tamales, such as Maseca

ingredients.name: Lard
ingredients.note: plus 1 tbsp for the sauce; or vegetable shortening

ingredients.name: Dried corn husks
ingredients.note: plus extra to line the steamer

instructions: Simmer the pork with the water, onion, 2 garlic cloves, bay leaves and 1 tsp salt, partly covered, about 2 hours, until it shreds easily. Strain and keep the broth (you need about 5 cups). Shred the pork.
While the pork cooks, soak the corn husks in a large bowl of hot water, weighed down with a plate, for at least an hour until soft and pliable.

Toast the chiles in a dry skillet a few seconds per side until fragrant, then soak in hot water 20 minutes. Drain and blend with the remaining 4 garlic cloves, cumin, oregano and 1 cup pork broth until smooth.

Heat 1 tbsp lard in a skillet, pour in the chile sauce (it splatters) and simmer 5 minutes. Stir in the shredded pork and salt to taste; it should be saucy, not soupy. Set aside 1/2 cup of sauce for the masa if you have extra.

Beat the 1 cup lard with a mixer for 2 to 3 minutes until fluffy. Mix the masa harina, baking powder and 2 tsp salt, then beat it in, alternating with about 3 1/2 cups warm broth, until soft like thick hummus. A small ball dropped in cold water should float; if not, beat a few minutes more.

Pat a husk dry, smooth side up and wide end toward you. Spread about 3 tbsp masa in a thin layer over the wide half, leaving a border on the sides. Spoon 1 1/2 tbsp pork down the middle, fold the sides over, then fold the narrow end up.

Stand the tamales open end up in a steamer basket lined with husks, snug but not packed tight. Add water below the basket, cover with more husks and a tight lid, and steam over medium heat about 1 1/2 hours, adding boiling water as needed.
They're done when the masa pulls cleanly away from the husk; let them rest 15 minutes so they firm up. Freeze extras in their husks and re-steam from frozen for about 30 minutes.

recipeDetails.title: Pan de Muerto
recipeDetails.summary: Soft, buttery sweet bread scented with orange and anise, topped with dough 'bones' and a shower of sugar. Allow about 2 1/2 hours of rising time.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: 1/2 cup for the dough, 1/4 cup for the top

ingredients.name: Eggs
ingredients.note: large, room temperature, plus 1 for brushing

ingredients.name: Orange blossom water
ingredients.note: in the Latin or Middle Eastern aisle; or 1 tsp vanilla

ingredients.name: Butter
ingredients.note: 8 softened for the dough, 2 melted for the top

instructions: In a stand mixer bowl, stir together the flour, 1/2 cup sugar, yeast, salt, anise seed and orange zest.
Add the warm milk, 3 eggs and orange blossom water. Mix with the dough hook on low until a shaggy dough forms, about 3 minutes.
With the mixer running, add the softened butter a tablespoon at a time. Knead on medium 8 to 10 minutes until smooth, elastic and slightly tacky. (By hand, knead about 15 minutes.)
Cover and let rise somewhere warm until doubled, 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Cut off about a quarter of the dough for decorating. Divide the rest in two, shape into smooth round loaves and set on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

For each loaf, roll 2 ropes of the reserved dough, pressing your fingers along them to make knobby 'bones', and lay them in a cross over the top. Roll a small ball and set it in the center. Beat the extra egg and brush it on to help everything stick.
Cover loosely and let rise 45 minutes until puffy. Heat the oven to 350°F. Brush again with egg and bake 30 to 35 minutes until deep golden; tent with foil if the bones brown too fast.
Brush the warm loaves with melted butter and sprinkle generously with the remaining sugar. Cool before slicing.

recipeDetails.title: Champurrado
recipeDetails.summary: A thick, warm chocolate drink made with masa, piloncillo and cinnamon, whisked until frothy. Lovely with pan de muerto or tamales.

ingredients.name: Masa harina
ingredients.note: instant corn masa flour, such as Maseca

ingredients.name: Whole milk
ingredients.note: or use more water, as many families do

ingredients.name: Piloncillo
ingredients.note: in the Latin aisle; or 1/2 cup packed dark brown sugar

ingredients.name: Cinnamon stick
ingredients.note: Mexican canela if you can find it

ingredients.name: Mexican chocolate
ingredients.note: one tablet, such as Ibarra or Abuelita, chopped

instructions: Whisk the masa harina into 2 cups of the water until completely smooth, with no lumps.
In a medium pot, heat the remaining 2 cups water, the milk, piloncillo and cinnamon stick over medium heat, stirring until the piloncillo dissolves, about 5 minutes.
Add the chocolate and stir until melted.

Pour the masa mixture through a sieve into the pot, whisking constantly. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook 10 to 12 minutes, whisking often so it doesn't stick, until it thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Take out the cinnamon stick, add the salt, and whisk hard (or use a molinillo) until frothy. Serve hot, thinning with a little milk or water if it gets too thick.

recipeDetails.title: Calabaza en Tacha
recipeDetails.summary: Pumpkin wedges slowly candied in a piloncillo syrup with cinnamon, cloves and orange peel until dark, glossy and spoon-tender. Serve warm or cold.

ingredients.name: Pie pumpkin
ingredients.note: sugar or pie pumpkin; kabocha or butternut squash also work

ingredients.name: Piloncillo
ingredients.note: in the Latin aisle; or 2 cups packed dark brown sugar plus 1 tbsp molasses

instructions: Scrub the pumpkin, cut it into large wedges about 3 inches wide, and scrape out the seeds and strings. Leave the skin on; it holds the pieces together.
In a large, wide pot, heat the water, piloncillo, cinnamon, cloves and orange peel over medium heat, stirring, until the piloncillo melts into a syrup, about 10 minutes.
Lay the pumpkin in the syrup flesh side down, snug in one or two layers. Cover and simmer on low 40 minutes, spooning syrup over the top now and then.

Turn the pieces skin side down, uncover, and keep simmering and basting 25 to 30 minutes, until the flesh is dark amber and very tender and the syrup is thick. Watch the end so the syrup doesn't burn.
Cool the pumpkin in its syrup. Serve warm or chilled with plenty of syrup; many families pour a little cold milk over it. Keeps a week in the fridge.

menus.reviewNotes: Built as a home cook's table rather than a definitive menu: mole with chicken and red pork tamales as the mains (both regularly placed on ofrendas and shared afterward), arroz rojo as the side mole needs, then pan de muerto, champurrado and calabaza en tacha as the sweets. Families vary a lot: Oaxacan households may make mole negro and tamales in banana leaf, others make green chicken or rajas-and-cheese tamales, Yucatán families bake mucbipollo, and pan de muerto toppings differ (sugar, sesame, red-tinted sugar); the intro says this. The mole is a manageable scratch version within the 20-ingredient limit and the last step openly notes that many cooks start from jarred paste. Left out: atole flavors beyond champurrado, sugar skulls (craft, not cooking), and the dead's favorite drinks such as mezcal, beer or Coca-Cola that often go on the ofrenda, since those are personal choices rather than recipes. No library recipe genuinely belonged (the Mexican library dishes are weeknight tacos and fajitas), so all six are new. I did not tag the mole or champurrado gluten-free/dairy-free because chocolate tablet brands vary. Dates: Día de Muertos is fixed on November 1–2 every year (no lookup needed); the window opens 10-18 so families can shop for chiles, husks and piloncillo and plan tamaladas, since ofrendas often go up from late October, and closes 11-03.

menus.title: A Diwali feast at home
menus.intro: Dishes many families make for Diwali: a rich paneer curry, puja-style potatoes and puris and South Indian lemon rice made without onion or garlic, plus kheer and besan ladoo. Festival food varies a lot between North and South Indian, Gujarati, Bengali, Sikh and Jain homes, so swap in your own family's favorites.

recipeDetails.title: Shahi Paneer
recipeDetails.summary: Soft paneer in a silky, mildly spiced cashew-tomato gravy finished with cream and cardamom. A rich, celebratory curry for the Diwali table.

ingredients.name: Paneer
ingredients.note: cut into 3/4-inch cubes; extra-firm tofu works for a dairy-light version

ingredients.name: Tomatoes
ingredients.note: roughly chopped, or one 14-oz can crushed tomatoes

ingredients.name: Green cardamom pods
ingredients.note: lightly crushed; or 1/4 tsp ground cardamom

ingredients.name: Kashmiri chili powder
ingredients.note: Indian grocery; or 3/4 tsp paprika plus a pinch of cayenne

ingredients.name: Kasuri methi
ingredients.note: dried fenugreek leaves, Indian grocery; leave out if you can't find it

instructions: Put the onion, garlic, ginger, tomatoes and cashews in a saucepan with 1 cup of the water. Cover and simmer 12 to 15 minutes, until the onion and cashews are soft.
Cool a few minutes, then blend until completely smooth. For an extra-silky gravy, push it through a sieve.
To make it without onion and garlic, as many families do for puja cooking, leave both out, add 2 more tablespoons of cashews and a pinch of asafoetida (hing) with the whole spices below.
Heat the ghee in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the cardamom and bay leaf and let them sizzle for 20 seconds.

Pour in the blended sauce (it will spatter) and the remaining 1/2 cup water. Stir in the chili powder and salt and simmer, stirring often, 10 to 12 minutes, until thick and glossy and the ghee starts to show at the edges.
Stir in the cream, sugar and garam masala, then add the paneer. Crush the kasuri methi between your palms over the pan and simmer gently 3 to 4 minutes, just until the paneer is hot.
Remove the bay leaf, taste for salt and garnish with cilantro. Serve with puris, naan or rice.

recipeDetails.title: Puja-Style Aloo Tamatar Sabzi
recipeDetails.summary: Soft potatoes in a thin, tangy tomato gravy seasoned with cumin, hing and ginger, made without onion or garlic. The classic partner for hot puris.

ingredients.name: Asafoetida
ingredients.note: hing, Indian grocery; many brands are cut with wheat flour, so check the label if avoiding gluten

ingredients.name: Serrano pepper
ingredients.note: slit lengthwise; or any green chili

ingredients.name: Kashmiri chili powder
ingredients.note: or 1/4 tsp paprika plus a pinch of cayenne

ingredients.name: Amchur
ingredients.note: dry mango powder, Indian grocery; or 1 tsp lemon juice

instructions: Boil the whole potatoes in salted water until a knife slides in easily, 20 to 25 minutes. Drain, cool slightly, peel and break into rough bite-size chunks with your hands.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds; when they sizzle and darken a shade, add the asafoetida, ginger and green chili and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, turmeric, coriander and chili powder. Cook, stirring, 6 to 8 minutes, until the tomatoes collapse and the oil starts to separate.
Add the potatoes and salt and stir to coat. Mash a few pieces against the side of the pot; they thicken the gravy.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then simmer 8 to 10 minutes. The gravy should stay loose enough to scoop with puri; add a splash of water if it gets thick.
Stir in the amchur and garam masala, taste for salt and finish with cilantro. Serve hot.

recipeDetails.title: Whole Wheat Puri
recipeDetails.summary: Small whole wheat breads that puff into golden balloons in hot oil. Fry them just before eating and serve with aloo sabzi, chole or kheer.

ingredients.name: Whole wheat flour
ingredients.note: Indian atta (chapati flour) is best; US whole wheat flour works, or use half all-purpose for softer puris

ingredients.name: Oil for deep frying
ingredients.note: any neutral oil, 2 to 3 inches deep in the pan

instructions: Mix the flour, semolina, salt and 1 tablespoon oil. Add water a little at a time, kneading into a firm, smooth dough, stiffer than chapati dough. Cover and rest 15 minutes.
Divide into 16 balls. Rub each with a drop of oil (not flour, which burns in the oil) and roll into 4-inch rounds of even thickness. Keep them covered as you go.
Heat the frying oil in a wok or heavy pot to 350 to 360°F. A pinch of dough should rise to the top at once.
Slide in one puri. As it floats, press it gently with the back of a slotted spoon so it puffs. Flip, fry 20 to 30 seconds more until golden, and lift out to drain on paper towels.
Fry the rest one or two at a time, letting the oil come back to temperature. Serve hot; they deflate as they cool but still taste good.

recipeDetails.title: South Indian Lemon Rice (Chitranna)
recipeDetails.summary: Cooked rice tossed with a crackling tempering of mustard seeds, dals, peanuts and curry leaves, brightened with lemon. Made with no onion or garlic.

ingredients.name: Cooked rice
ingredients.note: cooled; sona masoori is traditional, basmati or any long-grain works

ingredients.name: Chana dal
ingredients.note: split Bengal gram, Indian grocery; leave out if needed

ingredients.name: Urad dal
ingredients.note: split hulled black gram, Indian grocery; leave out if needed

ingredients.name: Curry leaves
ingredients.note: fresh, Indian grocery; no real substitute, leave out if you can't find them

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.note: grated; leave out for Jain cooking

ingredients.name: Asafoetida
ingredients.note: hing; check the label if avoiding gluten

instructions: Spread the rice on a tray to cool and loosen the grains; day-old rice works well.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and let them pop, then add the chana dal, urad dal and peanuts and stir until the dals turn golden, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the red chilies, green chili, curry leaves and ginger and stir 30 seconds (the leaves will spatter). Add the asafoetida and turmeric and turn off the heat.
Stir the lemon juice and salt into the warm tempering off the heat; cooked lemon juice turns bitter.
Add the rice and fold gently until every grain is yellow, without mashing. Taste for salt and lemon and finish with cilantro. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipeDetails.title: Rice Kheer with Cardamom and Saffron
recipeDetails.summary: Rice slowly simmered in whole milk until creamy, scented with cardamom and saffron and topped with almonds and pistachios. Good warm or chilled.

ingredients.name: Basmati rice
ingredients.note: rinsed and soaked 20 minutes; Bengali families often use fragrant gobindobhog rice for payesh

ingredients.name: Green cardamom pods
ingredients.note: seeds crushed; or 1/2 tsp ground cardamom

instructions: Bring the milk to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pot, stirring so it doesn't catch.

Drain the rice, lightly crush it between your fingers, and add it to the milk. Lower the heat and simmer, stirring every few minutes and scraping the bottom, 40 to 50 minutes, until the rice is very soft and the milk has reduced by about a third.
Stir in the sugar, cardamom and saffron with its milk and simmer 5 minutes more. Add the raisins if using.
Take off the heat and stir in most of the nuts. The kheer thickens as it cools; loosen with a little milk if needed.
Serve warm, or chill for a few hours or overnight, topped with the remaining nuts.

recipeDetails.title: Besan Ladoo
recipeDetails.summary: Chickpea flour slowly roasted in ghee until nutty, then mixed with sugar and cardamom and rolled into sweets. They keep for two weeks, so make them early.

ingredients.name: Chickpea flour
ingredients.note: besan, Indian grocery or the gluten-free aisle; coarse ladoo besan if you can find it

ingredients.name: Ghee
ingredients.note: melted, plus a little more if needed; Indian grocery or next to the butter

ingredients.name: Powdered sugar
ingredients.note: sifted; Indian bura or tagar is traditional

instructions: Melt the ghee in a heavy skillet over low heat. Add the chickpea flour and stir to combine; it will be thick and pasty at first.

Roast over low heat, stirring constantly and scraping the edges, 20 to 25 minutes. It is ready when it smells nutty, has turned deep golden, and loosens into a soft, flowing paste. Don't rush it with high heat: underroasted besan tastes raw and it scorches easily.
Transfer to a bowl and cool 10 to 15 minutes, until warm but no longer hot. If it is too hot, the sugar melts and the ladoos go flat.
Add the powdered sugar, cardamom and nuts and mix well with your hands.
Take a heaping tablespoon at a time and press and roll firmly into 16 smooth balls. If the mixture crumbles, work in a teaspoon of melted ghee.
Let them set 30 minutes. Store airtight at room temperature for up to 2 weeks.

menus.reviewNotes: Built as an all-vegetarian festival meal: a North Indian/Punjabi-style shahi paneer for richness, the puri-aloo pairing many households cook as the puja meal (the aloo sabzi uses hing and ginger, no onion or garlic), chitranna as a South Indian dish that is naturally free of onion and garlic, and two sweets: kheer (payesh in Bengali homes) and besan ladoo, which many families make days ahead and share. The paneer step explains how to make it without onion and garlic too. Second-cook review: the menu doesn't cover everything. Gujarati homes lean to farsan and sweets (mathiya, ghughra, mohanthal), South Indian Deepavali starts with an early oil bath and murukku, mysore pak or kesari, Bengali families mark Kali Puja the same night, and Sikh families celebrate Bandi Chhor Divas, often with karah prasad, langar-style dal and sabzi, and sweets. I left out namkeen and fried snacks (chakli, mathri, chivda) and dishes like kaju katli and gulab jamun that most US households buy rather than cook, so the menu stays cookable as one meal. Jain families avoid root vegetables, so the aloo sabzi doesn't suit them; the puri, lemon rice (ginger is optional) and both sweets do. Hing is often cut with wheat flour, so the hing dishes aren't tagged gluten-free. No mood tags were added. Dates: Lakshmi Puja (main Diwali day) falls on Nov 8 2026, Oct 29 2027 and Oct 17 2028. That matches what I remembered and was confirmed by web search (Wikipedia Lakshmi Puja, publicholidays.in, drikpanchang). Each window opens about 13 days before Lakshmi Puja, so it covers Dhanteras shopping and ladoo-making, and closes 2 days after, through Govardhan Puja and Bhai Dooj. US amavasya timing can shift observance by a day, and the window allows for that.

menus.title: A smaller Thanksgiving
menus.intro: The plates many families can't do without, sized for a table of six: a turkey breast instead of a whole bird, stuffing, gravy, cranberry sauce and pumpkin pie, with most of it made a day or two ahead.

recipeDetails.title: Herb-Roasted Turkey Breast
recipeDetails.summary: A turkey breast roasted under garlic-herb butter, juicy and ready in about an hour and a half, mostly in the oven. Plenty for six, with pan juices saved for the gravy.

ingredients.name: Turkey breast
ingredients.note: boneless, skin on; thaw a frozen one in the fridge for 2 days. A 5 to 6 lb bone-in breast works too (see step 4)

ingredients.name: Rosemary
ingredients.note: fresh, finely chopped, or 1 tsp dried

ingredients.name: Sage
ingredients.note: fresh, finely chopped, or 1 tsp dried rubbed sage

instructions: If you can, salt the turkey the night before: pat it dry, sprinkle all over with the salt, and leave it uncovered on a plate in the fridge. Otherwise, salt it now.
Heat the oven to 400°F. Pat the turkey dry and let it sit out while the oven heats. If a boneless breast is loose or flat, roll it and tie it with kitchen twine every 2 inches so it cooks evenly.
