Mash the butter with the garlic, herbs, lemon zest and pepper. Loosen the skin with your fingers and rub half the butter underneath it, then the rest over the top. Set the turkey skin side up in a roasting pan or ovenproof skillet, tuck the lemon halves beside it and pour the broth around it.

Roast, basting with the pan juices twice and adding a splash of water if the pan runs dry, until the thickest part reads 160°F on an instant-read thermometer: 55 to 70 minutes for boneless, about 1 1/2 to 2 hours for bone-in. If the skin browns too fast, lay foil loosely over the top.
Move the turkey to a board and rest it 15 to 20 minutes under loose foil; it will rise to about 165°F. Pour the pan juices into a measuring cup for the gravy, squeezing in the roasted lemon to taste.
Slice across the grain and serve with the gravy, or spoon a little of the pan juices over the slices.

recipeDetails.title: Sage and Celery Bread Stuffing
recipeDetails.summary: Classic baked stuffing (or dressing, depending on who's asking): dried bread cubes with butter-softened onion and celery, sage, thyme and broth, crisp on top and soft underneath.

ingredients.name: Sturdy white bread
ingredients.note: a loaf of country or French bread, cut into 3/4-inch cubes (about 12 cups); bagged unseasoned stuffing cubes work too

ingredients.name: Sage
ingredients.note: fresh, chopped, or 2 tsp dried rubbed sage

ingredients.name: Chicken broth
ingredients.note: use vegetable broth to make it vegetarian

ingredients.name: Breakfast sausage
ingredients.note: loose, browned and drained, if your family makes it with sausage

instructions: Dry the bread: leave the cubes out on sheet pans overnight, or bake them at 300°F for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring once, until dry but not browned. Stale bread soaks up broth without turning to mush.
Heat the oven to 375°F and butter a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and celery with a pinch of salt for 8 to 10 minutes, until soft but not browned. Stir in the sage and thyme for 30 seconds.
In a very large bowl, toss the bread with the vegetables and butter, the parsley, salt, pepper and the sausage if using.
Whisk the eggs with 2 cups of the broth and pour it over, tossing gently until the bread is evenly moist. Add the last 1/2 cup if it still looks dry; it should be damp, not soggy.
Spread it in the dish, cover with foil and bake 25 minutes. Uncover and bake 20 to 30 minutes more, until the top is golden and crisp at the edges.
To get ahead, assemble it up to a day before, cover and refrigerate, then add about 10 minutes to the covered bake.

recipeDetails.title: Make-Ahead Holiday Mashed Potatoes
recipeDetails.summary: Rich, creamy mashed potatoes with butter, warm milk and sour cream, made up to two days ahead and reheated, so the stovetop is free on the day.

ingredients.name: Butter
ingredients.note: plus 1 tbsp for the top if making ahead

instructions: Peel the potatoes, cut them into even 2-inch chunks and cover with cold water in a large pot. Salt the water well.
Bring to a boil and simmer 15 to 20 minutes, until a knife slides in with no resistance. Drain, return to the warm pot and let them steam dry over low heat for a minute.
Meanwhile, warm the milk and butter together until the butter melts.
Mash the potatoes with a masher or ricer (not a blender or food processor, which makes them gluey). Stir in the warm milk mixture, then the sour cream, salt and pepper. Taste and adjust.

Serve now, topped with chives. To make ahead, spread in a buttered baking dish, dot with butter, cover and refrigerate up to 2 days. Reheat covered at 350°F for 30 to 40 minutes, stirring once and adding a splash of milk if they look dry, or keep them warm in a slow cooker on low.

recipeDetails.title: Turkey Pan Gravy
recipeDetails.summary: Smooth, savory gravy made in the roasting pan from the turkey's juices, butter, flour and broth, ready while the turkey rests.

ingredients.name: Turkey pan juices
ingredients.note: from the roast turkey; make up the amount with broth if short

ingredients.name: Butter
ingredients.note: or fat skimmed from the pan juices

ingredients.name: All-purpose flour
ingredients.note: for gluten-free, skip it and whisk 2 tbsp cornstarch into the cold broth instead

ingredients.name: Thyme
ingredients.note: dried, or a few fresh sprigs

instructions: Let the pan juices settle for a few minutes, then spoon off the fat that rises to the top. Keep up to 3 tbsp of it in place of the butter if you like.

Set the roasting pan over medium heat (across two burners if it's large), or use a saucepan. Melt the butter or turkey fat, whisk in the flour and cook, whisking, 2 to 3 minutes until it smells toasty and turns light tan.
Slowly whisk in the pan juices and broth, scraping up the browned bits from the pan. Add the thyme.
Simmer 5 to 8 minutes, whisking often, until it coats a spoon. Thin with a splash of broth if it gets too thick.
Taste before you add salt, since the juices are already salted. Season with pepper, strain if you want it very smooth, and serve hot in a warmed gravy boat.

recipeDetails.title: From-Scratch Green Bean Casserole
recipeDetails.summary: Tender green beans in a creamy mushroom sauce made on the stove, baked under a crunchy layer of canned fried onions. No canned soup needed.

ingredients.name: Green beans
ingredients.note: fresh, trimmed and cut into 2-inch pieces, or 2 bags (12 oz) frozen cut green beans, thawed

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F. Boil the fresh green beans in salted water for 4 to 5 minutes, until bright and just tender, then drain and rinse under cold water. (Thawed frozen beans skip this step.)
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms with a pinch of salt for 6 to 8 minutes, until browned and their liquid is gone. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for a minute. Slowly stir in the broth, then the milk, and simmer 3 to 5 minutes until thick. Season with the salt and pepper.
Fold in the green beans and half the fried onions, and spread it in a 2-quart baking dish.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until bubbling. Scatter the rest of the fried onions over the top and bake 5 minutes more, until golden.

To make ahead, assemble without the onions, cover and refrigerate up to a day, then bake 10 minutes longer before adding the topping. For the shortcut many families grew up on, use a can of cream of mushroom soup and 3/4 cup milk in place of steps 2 and 3.

recipeDetails.title: Orange Cranberry Sauce
recipeDetails.summary: Fresh cranberries simmered with sugar and orange until they burst into a glossy, sweet-tart sauce. Ten minutes on the stove, and better made a few days ahead.

ingredients.name: Fresh cranberries
ingredients.note: one bag, rinsed; frozen work without thawing

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: add up to 1/4 cup more if you like it sweeter

ingredients.name: Orange
ingredients.note: zest and 1/2 cup juice; or use 1/2 cup bottled orange juice

instructions: Stir the sugar, orange juice, water and salt together in a medium saucepan and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Add the cranberries, lower the heat and simmer 10 to 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until most of the berries have popped and the sauce starts to thicken.
Take it off the heat and stir in the orange zest and the cinnamon if using. It will look loose but sets as it cools.
Cool, then cover and refrigerate. It keeps up to a week, so it's an easy job to finish days before. Serve cold or at room temperature.

recipeDetails.title: Classic Spiced Pumpkin Pie
recipeDetails.summary: Silky pumpkin custard with cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg and cloves in a flaky crust. Bake it the day before; it slices best fully cooled.

ingredients.name: Refrigerated pie crust
ingredients.note: for a 9-inch pie, or a homemade crust or frozen deep-dish shell

ingredients.name: Pumpkin puree
ingredients.note: one can; plain pumpkin, not pumpkin pie filling

ingredients.name: Ground cloves
ingredients.note: or use 2 1/2 tsp pumpkin pie spice for all four spices

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the lower third. Fit the crust into a 9-inch pie plate and crimp the edge. Chill it while you make the filling.
Whisk the pumpkin, brown sugar, spices and salt until smooth. Whisk in the eggs and yolk, then the evaporated milk.
Set the pie plate on a sheet pan and pour in the filling.

Bake 15 minutes, then lower the oven to 350°F and bake 35 to 45 minutes more, until the edges are set and the center still jiggles slightly when you nudge the pan. If the crust edge browns too fast, cover it with strips of foil.
Cool on a rack for at least 2 hours; the center finishes setting as it cools. Refrigerate once cool and serve chilled or at room temperature, with whipped cream.

menus.reviewNotes: Reviewed as a long-time Thanksgiving host. The live menu was missing the four things people notice first when they're absent (stuffing/dressing, gravy, cranberry sauce, pie), and closed on peach cobbler, a summer dessert and an odd Thanksgiving finish; generic sheet-pan vegetables and the plain sick-day mashed potatoes (2 tbsp butter, serves 4) didn't fit a holiday table for six either. New: stuffing, holiday mashed potatoes (make-ahead, serves 8), pan gravy that uses the turkey's own juices, from-scratch green bean casserole (with the canned-soup shortcut noted), orange cranberry sauce, pumpkin pie. Turkey kept its id and was improved: optional overnight dry brine, tie a loose roast, bone-in timing, foil if browning, and the pan juices are now saved for the gravy; times unchanged. The intro no longer says 'the classic plates' and names what's included. What families vary: Southern and many Black families make cornbread dressing, collards (library: southern-collard-greens-with-smoked-turkey), mac and cheese and sweet potato pie; candied yams or sweet potato casserole are common nearly everywhere; many tables add dishes from their own heritage (tamales, lumpia, rice dishes). With a 7-recipe cap I chose the most widely shared set and left sweet potatoes and rolls out; the stuffing notes vegetable broth (vegetarian) and optional sausage, and the gravy notes cornstarch for gluten-free. Dates: Thanksgiving is the fourth Thursday of November (Nov 22-28), so the yearly 11-15 to 11-28 window was kept as instructed; it opens 7-13 days ahead and in the earliest years (e.g. Nov 22) runs a few days past the holiday for leftovers.

menus.title: Hanukkah: Eight Nights of Oil
menus.intro: Dishes many Jewish families make for Hanukkah, when frying in oil remembers the oil that lasted eight nights: crisp latkes, slow-braised brisket and jelly-filled sufganiyot. It's all dairy-free so it works kosher-style, which is why the latkes come with applesauce instead of sour cream alongside the meat.

recipeDetails.title: Slow-Braised Brisket with Onions
recipeDetails.summary: A beef brisket braised low and slow on a deep bed of onions until it's fork-tender, with a sweet-savory gravy from the pan. Even better made a day ahead, sliced cold and reheated in its juices.

ingredients.name: Beef brisket
ingredients.note: first cut (flat), fat trimmed to about 1/4 inch; from a kosher butcher if you keep kosher

ingredients.name: Beef broth
ingredients.note: check the label is gluten-free if that matters to you

instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F. Pat the brisket dry and season both sides with the salt, pepper and paprika.
Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven or roasting pan over medium-high heat. Brown the brisket well, about 5 minutes per side, then set it on a plate.
Lower the heat to medium and add the onions with a pinch of salt. Cook, scraping up the browned bits, until soft and golden, about 12 minutes. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine, if using, and let it bubble for a minute. Add the broth, brown sugar, vinegar and bay leaves and stir.
Set the brisket fat side up on the onions, tuck the carrots around it, and spoon some onions over the top. Cover tightly with a lid or two layers of foil.
Braise 3 1/2 to 4 hours, until a fork slides in with almost no resistance. Check once halfway and add a splash of water if the liquid is low.

Rest the brisket 20 minutes, then slice thinly across the grain. Lay the slices back in the onions and gravy to serve. To make ahead, chill it whole overnight, lift off the fat, slice it cold and rewarm covered at 325°F for about 40 minutes.

recipeDetails.title: Crispy Potato Latkes
recipeDetails.summary: Potato and onion pancakes shallow-fried in oil until lacy and crisp. Dairy-free, so serve applesauce with a meat meal like brisket; save sour cream for a dairy night.

ingredients.name: Vegetable oil
ingredients.note: for shallow frying, or canola or peanut oil

instructions: Heat the oven to 250°F and set a wire rack on a baking sheet, so finished latkes stay hot and crisp while you fry the rest.
Grate the potatoes and onion on the large holes of a box grater or with the shredding disc of a food processor. Work quickly so the potatoes don't turn gray.
Pile the shreds onto a clean kitchen towel, gather it up and wring out as much liquid as you can over a bowl. Let the liquid sit 2 minutes, pour it off and keep the starch at the bottom.
Mix the potatoes and onion with the starch, eggs, matzo meal, salt, pepper and baking powder, if using.
Heat about 1/4 inch of oil in a large heavy skillet over medium-high heat until a shred of potato sizzles hard right away.
Drop in heaping 2-tablespoon mounds and flatten each to about 3 inches. Fry until deep golden and crisp, 3 to 4 minutes a side. Don't crowd the pan, and add oil between batches as needed.

Drain on paper towels for a moment, then move to the rack in the oven. Salt lightly and serve hot with applesauce. With a meat main, keep it to applesauce; on a dairy night, sour cream is the other favorite.

recipeDetails.title: Honey-Dill Roasted Carrots
recipeDetails.summary: Carrots roasted until caramelized, then glazed with honey and finished with fresh dill. A bright, easy side that bakes while the latkes fry, and it's dairy-free, so it sits fine beside brisket.
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the carrots with the oil, salt and pepper and spread them on a rimmed baking sheet with room between them.
Roast 20 minutes, until browned underneath, then turn them.
Drizzle with the honey, toss, and roast 8 to 10 minutes more, until tender and glazed at the edges.
Squeeze over the lemon, if using, scatter with the dill and serve warm or at room temperature.

recipeDetails.title: Sufganiyot (Jelly Doughnuts)
recipeDetails.summary: Yeast doughnuts fried in oil, filled with jam and dusted with powdered sugar. Made with water and oil, not milk or butter, so they can follow a brisket dinner.

ingredients.name: Instant yeast
ingredients.note: one packet; or active dry, bloomed in the water first

ingredients.name: Strawberry jam
ingredients.note: or raspberry jam, smooth or seedless pipes best

instructions: Whisk the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl. Add the warm water, eggs, 3 tablespoons oil and vanilla and mix into a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Knead 6 to 8 minutes by hand (or 5 minutes in a stand mixer with the dough hook) until smooth and springy. Cover and let rise in a warm spot until doubled, about 1 hour.

Roll the dough 1/2 inch thick on a floured counter and cut 2 1/2-inch rounds with a cutter or glass. Set them on a floured baking sheet, cover loosely and let rise 30 to 40 minutes, until puffy. Reroll scraps once.

Heat 2 to 3 inches of oil in a heavy pot to 350°F on a thermometer. Fry 3 or 4 at a time, about 1 1/2 minutes a side, until deep golden. Keep the oil between 340°F and 360°F, and drain on paper towels.
When they're cool enough to handle, poke a hole in the side of each with a chopstick or skewer and wiggle it to make a pocket.
Spoon the jam into a piping bag or zip-top bag with a corner snipped, and pipe about 2 teaspoons into each. Dust generously with powdered sugar and serve the same day.

menus.reviewNotes: Written as an Ashkenazi-American home cook: braised brisket on onions, shallow-fried potato latkes and Israeli-style sufganiyot are what most US Jewish families I know put out on at least one night. Everything is kept pareve apart from the brisket (latkes, carrots and sufganiyot made with water and oil, not milk or butter), so the meal works kosher-style; the latke recipe and intro say applesauce with meat, sour cream on a dairy night. Reused the library's warm-cinnamon-applesauce (apples, water, lemon, cinnamon, optional honey: pareve). Families vary a lot: brisket sweet with ketchup or onion-soup mix vs. savory with wine, sweet potato or zucchini latkes, Sephardi bimuelos or Italian-Jewish fried chicken, and dairy nights with cheese latkes or cheese for the Judith story. I left out cheese dishes to keep this one meal kosher-style, and left out kugel and roast chicken as less Hanukkah-specific. Dates: Hanukkah begins at sundown on Dec 4 2026 (to Dec 12), Dec 24 2027 (to Jan 1 2028) and Dec 12 2028 (to Dec 20), confirmed by web search (Wikipedia, Farmers' Almanac, calendarhours.com) and against 25 Kislev; each window opens 12 days before the first candle and closes a day after the last night. One window per Hanukkah from Oct 2026 through 2028.

menus.title: Christmas dinner at home
menus.intro: There are many Christmas tables in the US, from tamales and Nochebuena lechón to the Feast of the Seven Fishes and roast beef. This is one many families make for Christmas Day: a glazed ham, creamy potatoes, roasted Brussels sprouts and gingerbread cookies to bake together.

recipeDetails.title: Brown Sugar and Dijon Glazed Christmas Ham
recipeDetails.summary: A fully cooked spiral-cut ham warmed low and slow, then brushed with a brown sugar, orange and Dijon glaze until sticky and glossy. Most of the time is hands-off, and the leftovers carry you through the week.

ingredients.name: Spiral-cut ham
ingredients.note: bone-in, fully cooked; check the label if you need it gluten-free

ingredients.name: Orange juice
ingredients.note: plus 1/2 cup water for the pan

instructions: Take the ham out of the fridge an hour ahead. Heat the oven to 325°F and throw away the glaze packet if there is one.
Set the ham cut side down in a roasting pan, pour in 1/2 cup water, and cover the pan tightly with foil.
Bake about 12 minutes per pound (1 1/2 to 1 3/4 hours for 8 lb), until the center reads 120°F on an instant-read thermometer.
Meanwhile simmer the brown sugar, Dijon, orange juice, honey, cloves, cinnamon and pepper in a small saucepan for 5 minutes, stirring, until syrupy.

Uncover the ham, turn the oven up to 400°F, and brush half the glaze over it and between the slices. Bake 10 minutes, brush with the rest, and bake 10 to 15 minutes more, until glossy and the center reads 140°F.
Rest 15 minutes, then cut along the bone to free the slices. Spoon the pan juices over. Save the bone for split pea or bean soup.

recipeDetails.title: Creamy Scalloped Potatoes
recipeDetails.summary: Thin-sliced Yukon Golds baked in garlicky cream until tender inside and golden on top. They can be assembled in the morning and baked while the ham rests.

ingredients.name: Gruyère cheese
ingredients.note: grated; Swiss or white cheddar works too

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F and butter a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Warm the cream, milk, butter, garlic, thyme, nutmeg, salt and pepper in a large pot until steaming. Add the potato slices and simmer gently 8 to 10 minutes, stirring carefully so they don't stick, until just starting to soften and the cream thickens.
Pour into the dish and press the slices flat. Scatter the cheese on top if using.
Cover with foil and bake 30 minutes, then uncover and bake 30 to 35 minutes more, until bubbling, browned and a knife slides through easily.
Let it sit 10 to 15 minutes before serving so the cream sets.
To make ahead: assemble through step 3, cool, cover and refrigerate up to 8 hours; add 15 minutes to the covered bake.

recipeDetails.title: Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Cranberries and Pecans
recipeDetails.summary: Brussels sprouts roasted until the edges crisp, then tossed with dried cranberries, toasted pecans and a little maple and balsamic. Bright and a bit sweet next to the ham.
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the sprouts with the oil, salt and pepper on a large sheet pan and turn them cut side down. Use two pans if they're crowded.
Roast 20 to 25 minutes, until browned underneath and tender. Scatter the pecans on the pan for the last 5 minutes to toast.
Tip into a bowl and toss with the cranberries, maple syrup and balsamic. Taste for salt and serve warm or at room temperature.

recipeDetails.title: Soft Gingerbread Cut-Out Cookies
recipeDetails.summary: Spiced molasses cookies for cutting into people, stars and trees: soft in the middle, sturdy enough to decorate. Make the dough a day or two ahead and let the kids cut and frost.

ingredients.name: Powdered sugar
ingredients.note: for icing, whisked with 2 to 3 tbsp milk

instructions: Whisk the flour, ginger, cinnamon, cloves, baking soda and salt in a bowl.
Beat the butter and brown sugar until fluffy, about 2 minutes. Beat in the egg, molasses and vanilla.
Mix in the flour on low just until a soft dough forms. Divide in half, flatten into disks, wrap and chill at least 2 hours or up to 3 days.
Heat the oven to 350°F and line two baking sheets with parchment. Roll one disk 1/4 inch thick on a floured counter and cut out shapes; reroll the scraps once.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes, until the edges are set and the centers look just dry. Cool 5 minutes on the pan, then move to a rack.
Once completely cool, pipe or spread on the icing if using. Baked cookies keep a week in a tin; the dough freezes for 3 months.

menus.reviewNotes: Second-cook review: a glazed spiral ham with scalloped potatoes, a roasted green vegetable and gingerbread is a common US Christmas Day table and is doable for one home cook with one oven: ham reheats covered at 325°F, potatoes go in alongside and finish while the ham rests at 400°F, and the sprouts roast during that rest. Cookie dough is made days ahead. What families vary: roast beef or prime rib instead of ham, pineapple or cherry glazes, au gratin with more cheese, green bean casserole or glazed carrots, sugar cookies, pies or a bûche de Noël. Left out on purpose: Christmas Eve traditions (tamales, Nochebuena lechón, the Feast of the Seven Fishes, Polish Wigilia) are each a full table of their own and would make an incoherent mix next to a ham; the intro names them instead, and they would make good separate menus. No library or pack recipe fit well (simple-mashed-potatoes and sheet-pan-roasted-vegetables are weeknight-plain), so all four are new. Mood tags: only comfort-food and cozy-night-in on the scalloped potatoes (served warm, 100 min total); none elsewhere. Dates: Christmas is fixed on December 25, so a yearly window 12-10 to 12-26 covers about two weeks of planning and shopping, Christmas Eve, and the day after; no web lookup was needed.

menus.title: Kwanzaa Karamu feast
menus.intro: Karamu, the Kwanzaa feast on December 31, gathers family and friends around food from Africa and across its diaspora. These are dishes many families bring to the table, from West African jollof and groundnut stew to Southern collards, black-eyed peas and sweet potato pie, and every household's spread looks a little different.

recipeDetails.title: Kelewele (Ghanaian Spiced Fried Plantains)
recipeDetails.summary: Very ripe plantains tossed in fresh ginger, onion and cayenne, then pan-fried until caramelized at the edges. Sweet, peppery and gone fast; ease off the cayenne for kids.

ingredients.name: Plantains
ingredients.note: very ripe, skins mostly black; in the produce aisle of most supermarkets and at Latin, Caribbean or African markets

ingredients.name: Cayenne pepper
ingredients.note: or a pinch of minced Scotch bonnet; use less for kids

ingredients.name: Ground nutmeg
ingredients.note: some families add a pinch of cloves or anise instead

instructions: Cut off both ends of each plantain, slit the skin lengthwise and peel it away. Cut the plantains into 1-inch chunks or thick diagonal slices.
In a bowl, mix the ginger, grated onion, cayenne, salt and nutmeg if using. Add the plantains and toss until every piece is coated. Let them sit 10 minutes while the oil heats.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat until a piece of plantain sizzles as soon as it goes in.
Fry the plantains in a single layer, in batches, 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden brown with dark caramelized edges. Turn the heat down if they darken before they soften.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm, with roasted peanuts on the side if you like.

recipeDetails.title: Southern Sweet Potato Pie
recipeDetails.summary: A silky, spiced sweet potato filling in a flaky crust, the pie many Black families bake for every holiday table. Bake it the day before; it slices best at room temperature.

ingredients.name: Refrigerated pie crust
ingredients.note: one 9-inch crust, unbaked, or your own homemade crust

ingredients.name: Ground nutmeg
ingredients.note: freshly grated if you have it

ingredients.name: Lemon juice
ingredients.note: a family touch in some kitchens, to brighten the filling

instructions: Put the whole, unpeeled sweet potatoes in a pot, cover with water and boil 40 to 45 minutes, until a knife slides through the center. Drain and let them cool enough to handle.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Fit the crust into a 9-inch pie plate and crimp the edge.
Slip the skins off the sweet potatoes and beat the flesh with the butter until smooth, about 2 minutes with a hand mixer. Pick out any stringy fibers that wrap around the beaters.
Beat in both sugars, the evaporated milk, eggs, vanilla, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt and lemon juice if using, until the filling is silky.
Pour the filling into the crust and smooth the top. Bake 55 to 60 minutes, until the edges are set and the center jiggles only slightly. Cover the crust edge with foil if it browns too fast.
Cool on a rack at least 2 hours before slicing. Serve at room temperature, with whipped cream if you like. It keeps, covered, in the fridge for 3 days.

menus.reviewNotes: Kwanzaa is a cultural (not religious) week-long celebration, 26 December to 1 January; Karamu is held on 31 December, so this is a fixed-date window (12-14 to 01-01, wrapping the new year) to give two weeks for planning and shopping. Dates are fixed by the holiday's founding, so no lookup was needed; no religious claims are made. The menu deliberately mixes West African dishes (groundnut stew, jollof, kelewele) with the African American Southern table (collards, Hoppin' John, cornbread, sweet potato pie), which is how many Karamu spreads look; Hoppin' John also nods to the New Year's Day black-eyed peas tradition that falls the next day. Families vary a lot: many add a Caribbean dish (jerk or curry chicken, rice and peas), fried fish or catfish, mac and cheese, or bean pie, and some Karamu are potlucks. I left out mac and cheese and a second main to keep it at seven dishes, and didn't add mood tags to the new recipes. The cuisine id for Southern is 'southern' (the brief's 'southern-soul' is not a valid id). Two rice dishes (jollof and Hoppin' John) is intentional at a feast table, but a household could swap Hoppin' John for the pack's red-red to keep it to one.
